evidence.text: NIO absorbed a RMB 10,000/vehicle purchase-tax subsidy on ES8 orders locked through 30 April 2026 and then discontinued it mid-Q2 — Deutsche Bank named that discontinuation as a cause of the June ES8 order shortfall. ES8 (Gen 3) was 33,474 units of Q2's 107,658, so removing RMB 10,000/unit from even ~18,000 Q2 deliveries retains ~RMB 180m of margin, which is the whole of Deutsche Bank's ~RMB 180m Q2 non-GAAP net income estimate. The 2.1% unit miss versus the 110-115k guide was in part the price paid for that margin, not purely demand weakness.
evidence.why_not_priced: The delivery miss is a published monthly number every terminal has; the subsidy withdrawal that partly caused it is a line item disclosed only in Chinese-language promo terms and a CnEVPost analyst note, and it works in the opposite direction on the P&L. If the market had joined the two, the stock would not be sitting at its 52-week low on a 'profitability doubt' narrative into a quarter where the per-unit subsidy drag was actively being removed — you would see previews framing the unit miss as margin-accretive, and there are none.
evidence.independence: Overlaps with finding 2 (both are opex/margin mechanisms behind the profitability run) but is a separate line of the P&L. Corroborated independently by the 2026-04-02 CnEVPost piece documenting the RMB 10,000 ES8 purchase-tax subsidy and its 30 April cutoff: https://cnevpost.com/2026/04/02/nio-es8-deliveries-16255-mar-2026/

evidence.text: NIO's 20-F for FY2025, filed 2026-04-10, discloses that headcount fell to 35,032 from 45,635 — 10,603 jobs, the sharpest single-year cut in its history — with product and software development down 40% to 6,912 from 11,528 and 'user experience' (sales, marketing, service) down 30.8% to 16,885 from 24,410. NIO never gave aggregate numbers during 2025, calling it 'organizational optimization'. Q2 2026 volume was +29% sequentially (107,658 vs 83,465) against that reduced cost base.
evidence.why_not_priced: The aggregate figures exist only in an employee table deep in a 20-F; the wire coverage of that filing (StockTitan, Yahoo) carried the headline 'NIO files its annual report' with no headcount content, and the only outlets that extracted the numbers were a niche EV site and a LinkedIn post. If this were priced you would see it in the preview arithmetic as an explicit opex step-down, and consensus would not still be modelling a full-year loss of CN¥1.69/share. The negative tail is real too: cutting sales and service headcount 31% while launching two brands is a demand-execution risk, which is why the band spans zero.
evidence.independence: Partially overlaps finding 1 (both explain the profitability turn). Independent secondary extraction of the same table: https://eletric-vehicles.com/nio/nio-discloses-10600-job-cuts-in-2025-with-40-of-rd-staff-eliminated/

evidence.text: NIO's year-on-year growth rate collapses mechanically from the August number onward on base effects, and 1 September is NIO's established monthly-delivery publication slot, so the August figure plausibly lands in the same tape as Q2 results and the Q3 guide. July 2026 was 35,934, +71.0% YoY against a July 2025 base of ~21,017. But August 2025 was 31,305 and September 2025 was 34,749 (Q3 2025 total 87,071) — the base steps up ~49% in one month. Bottom-up August 2026 indicators point to roughly flat-to-modestly-up sequentially (third-gen ES8's latest 10,000 units took 30 days as of 21 August; Onvo L60 at 3,201 units in the first 28 days), implying Q3 near 113-118k and YoY growth roughly halving to ~+30%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sell-side has these comps; the marginal holder of a $4.37 ADS does not, and the narrative in circulation is the '+71% year-on-year' July headline. The structural half of this is the sharper point: NIO filed monthly delivery 6-Ks on 2026-06-01, 2026-07-02 and 2026-08-03 for the prior month, so 1 September is the slot for August, and no aggregator flags that this print carries three releases at once. If the market had this, the front-expiry implied move would sit above the 9.76% single-event level to reflect a compound catalyst, and the put/call open interest ratio would not be 0.32.
evidence.independence: Independent of findings 1, 2 and 4. Corroborated by the July 2026 delivery release (35,934, +71.0%): https://cnevpost.com/2026/08/01/nio-deliveries-jul-2026/ and the 6-K filing-date cadence on EDGAR.

evidence.text: NIO's smart-driving chief Ren Shaoqing has founded a separately registered embodied-AI/physical-AI-foundation-model company that has already reached a unicorn-level valuation, and NIO reportedly plans to make a strategic investment in it while Ren stays on as NIO's smart-driving chief. Reported 21 and 24 August 2026, after NIO's last public communication.
evidence.why_not_priced: It broke in Chinese-language and China-EV trade press in the nine days before the print and has no US wire pickup; NIO has not confirmed it and it is not in any filing. It is a divided-attention and related-party-transaction question in the single most valuation-sensitive function, and it is the kind of item that gets asked on the 8:00 a.m. call rather than in the release. If it were priced there would be a sell-side note on smart-driving key-man risk; there is none. Sign is genuinely ambiguous — on a $4 stock with calls bid, a robotics affiliation can be read as a positive optionality headline, which is why the band crosses zero.
evidence.independence: Independent of all other findings. Second, earlier report of the same facts from a different angle: https://cnevpost.com/2026/08/21/nio-ren-shaoqing-ventures-into-embodied-robotics-report/

evidence.text: NIO has now missed its own delivery guidance in consecutive disclosures — June 2026 came in at 40,597 against a 42,900-47,900 guide, and Q2 at 107,658 against 110,000-115,000 — so whatever Q3 unit and revenue range management gives on 1 September starts with an impaired discount factor.
evidence.why_not_priced: Weakest of the five and closest to priced — the individual misses are public. What is not in the coverage is that they are consecutive and both attributable to NIO's own promotional withdrawals rather than to the market, which changes how a fresh guide should be read. Sized small precisely because most of this is in the -9.2% twenty-day drift already.
evidence.independence: Overlaps finding 1, which supplies the mechanism for both misses. Q2 guide range and actual also in the same release.

evidence.text: Heidmar's earnings releases are the mechanical trigger for refreshing the resale prospectus covering 11,080,332 shares for B. Riley Principal Capital II: the 424B3 filed 2026-03-24 exists solely to supplement the 20 June 2025 prospectus 'with the information contained in our report on Form 6-K, filed with the SEC on March 24, 2026' - the same day as the Q4 print. The same pattern holds for 2025-08-12 (two 424B3s the day after the 2025-08-11 print), 2025-09-29 (424B3 and 6-K same day) and 2025-11-06, and a POS AM followed the Q1 print by two days. That resale registration was re-declared effective 2026-06-10, so 2026-09-01 is the first print under the refreshed shelf, and 11,080,332 shares is 170% of the company's entire non-affiliate share count.
evidence.why_not_priced: The baseline records 5 of 6 prints closing down with a 5.13% median reaction but explicitly sets history_usable to 0 and discounts the pattern as possibly describing a dead reporting regime. Nobody has supplied the mechanism, and the mechanism is what makes the pattern forward-looking rather than sample noise. If the market had focused on it there would be visible pre-print weakness in the last five sessions beyond the observed -1.42%, a discount to the sector's Q2 re-rating rather than a 24% 20-day run-up, and the covering analysts would be flagging equity-line dilution rather than modelling flat revenue. No 424B3 or draw disclosure exists yet for Q2, so the size of the refresh is unknown to holders.
evidence.independence: Overlaps with the float finding (same 6,498,572 non-affiliate denominator). Independently corroborated by the POS AM's own risk language and by management's Q1 call statement that it kept 'the ELOC live' but had not used it because '$1.27' levels were not 'reflective of the company's valuation' - the stock is now $1.38, above that bar: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-heidmar-maritime-q1-2026-sees-revenue-beat-stock-dips-93CH-4712449

evidence.text: The two-analyst FY2026 revenue forecast of $74.29m implies roughly $18.6m per quarter for Q2-Q4 against Q1 2026 actual of $18.4m - i.e. essentially flat, and below Q4 2025's $25.1m - while the spot rates that drive both of Heidmar's revenue lines rose 47-82% sequentially in Q2 (Frontline realised VLCC $103,500 to $152,700/day, Suezmax $72,400 to $111,500/day, LR2/Aframax $50,700 to $92,400/day, Q1 to Q2 2026), and the five vessels added in March/April 2026 contribute a full quarter for the first time. Heidmar's Q1 revenue was $5.68m trade revenues plus $12.67m voyage and time charter revenues from eight vessels employed on short-term spot/TC voyages versus one a year earlier; the Q2 2025 comparative is $9.6m total revenue and $0.5m adjusted net income.
evidence.why_not_priced: The rate data is public but the translation into this company's gross-freight-linked P&L is not: this name has one to two covering analysts who got Q1 exactly backwards (revenue below estimate, EPS beat by roughly 1,000%), demonstrating they do not model the structure. If the gap were priced the FY2026 revenue line would have been revised above Q4 2025's run-rate after the peer prints of the last three weeks, and HMR's 20-day move would look like a tanker-equity re-rating rather than -15% from its own 52-week high. snippet_only on the Frontline TCE figures (globenewswire returned 503 to direct fetch; figures taken from search snippet of that release).
evidence.independence: Independently corroborated by SFL's Q2 2026 report (Suezmax spot TCE ~$133,000/day) and Okeanis Eco Tankers Q2 2026 (Suezmax $174,900/day): https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/26/sfl-sfl-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

evidence.text: Heidmar's fee-earning commercially managed fleet was effectively flat through Q2 2026: the 2025 Form 20-F filed 2026-04-30 states 'The Capital vessels compose 25 of the 49 vessels currently managed by Heidmar', while the 2026-07-07 release states the company manages 'around 50 vessels under commercial management and 16 vessels under technical management' - and that is after an acquisition (Q-Shipping B.V., effective 2026-07-01) that the company itself says added nine vessels to the managed fleet. Heidmar has issued no fleet-addition press release since 2026-05-19, the longest such gap since the de-SPAC, against five additions announced for Q1.
evidence.why_not_priced: This requires putting two documents filed ten weeks apart side by side; neither figure is a headline and no aggregator carries a vessel-count time series for this name. If it were priced the equity would not have run 24% in 20 days on a platform-growth narrative, and the sell-side FY revenue number would show a decelerating vessel-count assumption rather than a flat one. The count as at 30 June is not public and will be disclosed for the first time tomorrow.
evidence.independence: Cross-checked against the 2026-07-07 Q-Shipping release's own fleet counts: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/07/3323069/0/en/Heidmar-Maritime-Holdings-Corp-Expands-Ship-Management-Platform.html

evidence.text: Heidmar has had no Chief Financial Officer since 31 May 2026 - Niki Fotiou ceased in the role and CEO Pankaj Khanna took over 'the finance function' pending a search - and no successor has been announced as of 2026-08-31, three months later. Q2 2026 is therefore the first quarter this company has closed, audited-reviewed and reported without a CFO. Separately, Heidmar has furnished no Form 6-K since 2026-05-28 despite three subsequent material announcements (CFO departure, Nasdaq compliance regained, Q-Shipping acquisition).
evidence.why_not_priced: The June departure was press-released and is stale news; what is not priced is the three-month absence of a replacement and the fact that this print is the first one produced without a CFO, which raises the odds of thin disclosure, no quantitative outlook, and a call at which the CEO answers financial questions alone. If holders had focused on it the stock would not have re-rated 24% into the print, and the coverage would carry a governance discount rather than a growth multiple. The vacancy is verifiable only by absence - there is no announcement to aggregate.
evidence.independence: Independently confirmed by the SEC filing index, which shows no 6-K after 2026-05-28 and no Form 3 or 6-K appointing a CFO: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002029471.json

evidence.text: Only 6,498,572 of Heidmar's 58,991,997 outstanding shares are held by non-affiliates - an 11.0% float worth about $9.0m at spot - against 20-day average volume of 50,189 shares and short interest of just 127,609 shares. The prospectus states verbatim: 'As of May 20, 2026, we had 58,991,997 Common Shares outstanding, of which 6,498,572 shares were held by non-affiliates of our company.'
evidence.why_not_priced: The number sits on an inside page of a post-effective amendment, not on any quote page; every screener reports the 58.99m share count and a float five to nine times the true one. It is not directionally priced because it cannot be - it is a convexity fact, and the baseline has no option chain at all with which to express it, so nothing in the price states a reaction width. Negligible short interest (1.9% of float) also means there is no crowded position to unwind, so a genuine beat has no natural seller.
evidence.independence: Short interest figure from a different source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/hmr/statistics/

evidence.text: Three Heidmar directors filed Form 144s to sell 244,862 shares between 2026-06-11 and 2026-07-06 - Andreas Konialidis 113,287 shares ($165,400), Vasileios Loutradis 126,575 shares ($138,699) and Andre Lockhorst 5,000 shares ($5,950) - equal to about 3.8% of the entire non-affiliate float and roughly five sessions of average volume. If this had registered with holders, the 24% 20-day run-up would have met visible insider supply in the tape and the coverage would mention it. evidence.text: Half of Heidmar's fee base sits with one related party that has just been separately capitalised: the 20-F states the Capital vessels are 25 of 49 managed vessels and 'accounted for 37% of our total revenues from the Pools during the year ended December 31, 2025', and Capital Tankers Corp. listed on Euronext Growth Oslo on 2026-03-17 after raising about USD 500m, with a fleet of 30 super-eco crude tankers of which 21 are newbuildings delivering 2026-2028 plus options on 13 more.

evidence.text: The syndicated Q1 FY27 consensus revenue of $9.47bn (+10.4% on the $8,578m year-ago base) sits roughly a point below what Medtronic's own 3 June quarterly guidance implies — 11.5% to 12.0% organic growth plus a 'neutral to $50 million' FX tailwind plus acquired revenue from CathWorks/Scientia/SPR, i.e. about $9.55-9.65bn — while consensus EPS of $1.39 is exactly the midpoint of the guided $1.38-$1.40; the same one-point gap exists at the full-year level ($38.85bn consensus vs 6.75-7.25% organic on $36,364m plus 0-1% FX plus M&A). The likeliest cause is incomplete modelling of the 53rd selling week, which management [sizing note removed]. Mechanically this makes a print that merely lands on guidance read in the wire copy as a $100-180m top-line beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes the reconciliation of a consensus print against the company's own quarterly guide, and the inconsistency is visible only as an internal contradiction in the estimate set (EPS on guidance, revenue below it). If it were priced, previews would be flagging a 'low bar on revenue' rather than quoting the $9.47bn as the bar; instead Zacks' preview quotes it straight. I keep the size small and let the band cross zero because the marginal holder of a mega-cap trades the buy-side bar, not the Zacks bar, and MDT has twice in the last four prints sold off on a headline beat.
evidence.independence: Overlaps only in direction with the Needham note (PT $101 to $114, expects a beat and a guidance raise, https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/needham-raises-medtronic-stock-price-target-on-product-cycle-93CH-4879312); the arithmetic itself is independent of any broker note and rests on the transcript plus the $8,578m base in the 2025-08-19 release.

evidence.text: As of 2026-08-31 no registration statement or tender-offer document for the MiniMed split-off exists on EDGAR: Medtronic (CIK 1613103) has filed no 8-K since 2026-06-03 and no S-4/Schedule TO, and MiniMed Group (CIK 2062583) shows no S-4, S-1, 425 or SC TO on or after 2026-06-01. On 3 June management said separation was expected 'prior to year-end' and explicitly framed early separation as potential upside to FY27 guidance, which assumes twelve months of Diabetes consolidation. An exchange offer needs a registered offer document and a ~20-business-day offer period, so with nothing on file at end-August the 'upside from early separation' has not begun to be executed. Compounding it, MMED traded at $18.92 on 2026-08-26, below its $20.00 March IPO price, which weakens the discount economics of a split-off and raises the odds of a plain pro-rata spin-off that would retire none of Medtronic's ~1.28bn shares.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is an absence, and absences do not generate wire copy — there is no article saying 'Medtronic has not yet filed the exchange-offer S-4'. If the market had priced a slip, previews would be discussing whether FY27 guidance gets re-based rather than repeating the June 'full twelve months of Diabetes' framing. The band crosses zero because the standard sequencing is to launch an exchange offer immediately after a quarterly release, so the same fact can flip to a positive on 1 September.
evidence.independence: Cross-checked against Medtronic's own EDGAR index (no 8-K since 2026-06-03, https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001613103&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=60) and against the 2026-08-17 DEF 14A, whose only capital resolution is the routine annual 'overseas market purchases' authority, with no off-market purchase or exchange-offer resolution for the 15 October AGM.

evidence.text: The Investor Day Medtronic committed to on 2025-08-19, when it added two Elliott-adjacent directors and formed the Growth and Operating Committees, was promised for 'mid-calendar year 2026' and was to lay out the go-forward financial algorithm and the committees' margin and efficiency targets. Mid-2026 has passed and, as of 2026-08-31, no date has been announced: the June Q4 call did not mention it and the Medtronic newsroom shows only three releases since (21 July Touch Surgery Aide, 6 August Affera CE Mark, 20 August dividend).
evidence.why_not_priced: A missed soft deadline on an event with no announced date produces no headline and no estimate revision, so there is nothing for the tape to have reflected. If it were priced you would see notes handicapping the margin target, as happened around every peer's activist-driven capital markets day. The 1 September call is the natural venue to set a date, so the sign is genuinely two-sided and the band is wide.
evidence.independence: Independent of the other findings. Corroborated only by absence: the Medtronic newsroom listing through 2026-08-20 (https://news.medtronic.com/) contains no Investor Day announcement.

evidence.text: Boston Scientific reported on 2026-07-29 that its electrophysiology business grew only 3% in the US in calendar Q2 2026 (versus 23% internationally), citing competitive pressure and noting that US PFA is now roughly 80% of the AFib market. Calendar Q2 covers about two-thirds of Medtronic's fiscal Q1 (25 April to 31 July), and Cardiac Ablation Solutions — up 78% globally and 124% in the US in Medtronic's Q4 FY26 — is the single largest contributor to the 6.75-7.25% FY27 organic guide. The datapoint reads as continued Affera/Sphere-9 share gain in the quarter Medtronic is about to report, but the same disclosure caps how much market growth is left.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced, and I am sizing it accordingly. MDT rose 3.2% on 27-28 July, i.e. before the BSX print, and only 0.8% on 29 July itself, so the tape does not look like it repriced Medtronic's CAS line on the read-across. But the 80%-penetration remark is the bearish half of the same disclosure and cuts the other way, which is exactly why a single number here is not worth more than a few tenths.
evidence.independence: Overlaps with nothing else I found; the Affera CE Mark expansion for ventricular arrhythmias on 2026-08-06 (https://news.medtronic.com/) points the same way on the franchise but is a European label, not a US volume datapoint.

Tariffs: the Section 232 medical devices/supplies investigation opened 24 September 2025 is still unresolved as of August 2026, so the $250m FY27 / $75m Q1 COGS assumption has no new input either way

evidence.text: MMED's short interest is 5,896,696 shares at the 2026-08-14 settlement against a public float of 27.96m shares (Medtronic holds ~90% of 280.84m shares outstanding) - i.e. ~21% of float with 5.1-5.7 days to cover - yet the most widely syndicated short-interest pages display it as '2.1% of float' because they divide by shares outstanding rather than float; the position was built from 1,341,393 shares at the 2026-03-13 settlement to a 6,570,728 peak on 2026-06-30 and has been reduced only ~10% since, while the stock has roughly doubled off its 2026-05-15 low of $10.65.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no functioning listed market in which to express this: total option open interest is 833 contracts and the ATM bid-ask is 174% of mid, so the +22 vol-point 25-delta skew is a scarcity/hedging artifact in a 28m-share float rather than a statement of informed bearishness - if a real bearish consensus were priced you would also see it in the sell-side, which is 13 analysts at Strong Buy with BofA raising its target to $24 in mid-August. And the screen figure marginal holders actually read says 2.1%, not 21%, so the crowding is invisible at the point of decision.
evidence.independence: stockanalysis.com computes the float-adjusted figure correctly at 21.09% of float, 5.08 days to cover, float 27.96m, same 5.90m shares - https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mmed/statistics/ (2026-08-31). The float itself is independently established by the IPO size (28.0m shares) and Medtronic's 90.03% retained stake.

evidence.text: The IPO lock-up lapses on the morning of the print: the 424B4 is dated 2026-03-05 and EDGAR full-text search confirms it contains the phrase '180 days after the date of this prospectus' (180 days from 2026-03-05 is 2026-09-01), and that lock-up binds Medtronic's ~252.9m shares as well as every officer and director; as of 2026-08-31 Medtronic's EDGAR submissions show no S-4, no Schedule TO and no 425 has ever been filed, so the split-off exchange offer is not launched and becomes launchable from this print forward against a stated intent to finish the separation in calendar 2026.
evidence.why_not_priced: The coincidence of dates is arithmetic nobody publishes: MMED reports at 3:45 a.m. PDT on the exact day the restricted period ends, and the same morning Medtronic reports and could file the S-4/TO under Rule 162 early commencement. In a split-off exchange offer the arbitrage is long parent / short subsidiary, so announcement day is mechanically negative for MMED. If this were priced you would see it in the borrow and in front-expiry put open interest, and instead total OI across the whole 2026-09-18 chain is 833 contracts. You would also see the stock discounted, and instead it sits 3.5% off its 52-week high. Coverage frames the separation as a positive de-overhang event and does not date the launch window.
evidence.independence: Medtronic's own 2026-06-03 release still says 'a final decision has not been reached at this time' on structure - https://news.medtronic.com/2026-06-03-Medtronic-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2026-results-delivers-highest-annual-revenue-growth-in-10-years - and MMED's 2026-08-21 DEF 14A adds that 'Medtronic has no obligation to pursue or consummate any further dispositions... by any specified date or at all', which widens the band in both directions. Overlaps with finding 1 only insofar as an exchange offer would give existing shorts a delivery route rather than a buy-in.

evidence.text: MiniMed's Senior VP, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, Courtney Nelson Wills, notified the company on 2026-07-30 that she is resigning effective 2026-09-25 after an eight-week transition - disclosed in an 8-K filed 2026-08-05, i.e. she departs inside the exact window in which a tax-free split-off exchange offer, an S-4 and ~160 Medtronic transition-services agreements have to be executed.
evidence.why_not_priced: An item 5.02 8-K on a non-Section-16-headline officer at a six-month-old 28m-float carve-out generates no wire coverage and no analyst note; the stock rose over the following three weeks, which is what you would expect if nobody read it. If it were priced there would be a downgrade or at least a note naming legal-execution risk on the split-off. Her own Form 4 for 2026-07-31 shows 136,384 shares held, so this is not a token role.
evidence.independence: Her Form 4 of 2026-08-04 (transaction date 2026-07-31, code F, 1,762 shares withheld at $18.15) independently confirms she was still an active officer through quarter end and gives the holding size - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2062583/000211047726000004/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1785879853.xml. Otherwise independent of findings 1 and 2 except that it bears on the same separation timetable.

evidence.text: Q1 FY27 is a 14-week quarter and the two halves of the arithmetic sit in two different companies' disclosures: MiniMed's CFO said on 2026-06-03 that 'excluding the extra week, we expect Q1 growth to be roughly similar to Q4' (Q4 FY26 organic was 8.7%), while Medtronic's CFO quantified the extra selling week as '500 to 600 basis points to first-quarter growth' - stacking them implies MMED prints roughly 14% organic growth, versus the '~10% organic FY27 outlook' that quote pages and screens carry as the company's guidance.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 500-600bp Q1 quantification exists only in Medtronic's guidance, never in MiniMed's; MiniMed disclosed only the 1.0-1.5% full-year effect. Nasdaq shows a single estimate for MMED and stockanalysis.com carries no quarterly estimate at all, only the FY2027 annual $3.42bn. That is the signature of a name where the headline growth number is not modelled at the quarter level, so a ~14% organic print reads as a large acceleration against a '10%' anchor to exactly the momentum and retail flow that a 28m float is most sensitive to. If this were priced there would be a published quarterly consensus above the FY run-rate and a preview note explaining the 53rd week.
evidence.independence: MiniMed's CFO quote is separately reproduced by two transcript vendors - https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-6-3-mmed-stock/ and https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-minimed-sees-strong-q4-2026-growth-stock-rises-93CH-4724579 - and the 14-week quarter is corroborated by the fiscal dates themselves (FY26 ended 2026-04-24 per the 10-K, Q1 FY27 ended 2026-07-31). Partly offset by the same call's disclosure that Flex had only 'four to six weeks of selling in Q1'.

A second Blackstone milestone charge in Q1 FY27: the $157m charge on MiniMed Flex hit fiscal Q4 FY26 and Medtronic stated the agreement 'is not expected to have an impact on Medtronic's results in its 2027 fiscal year' (medtechdive, 2026-03-25), which kills the recurring-charge thesis for this print.

MiniMed's fiscal Q1 FY27 is a 98-day (14-week) quarter — 2026-04-25 through 2026-07-31 — against a 91-day (13-week) prior-year quarter (2025-04-26 through 2025-07-25); the entire 53rd week of FY27 falls in this single quarter, and MiniMed's own definition of 'Organic Revenue Growth' adjusts only for FX and Italian payback accruals, NOT for extra weeks, so the organic-growth headline will print roughly double the 8.7% it printed for Q4 FY26 on calendar alone. The dates are established by the company's own filings: FY26 ended 2026-04-24 (Q4 exhibit 99.1), the year-ago quarter ended 2025-07-25 (Medtronic 10-Q mdt-20250725), and this quarter ends 2026-07-31 (the 2026-07-20 announcement).
evidence.why_not_priced: Management pre-guided the arithmetic on the 3 June call, so the five covering analysts almost certainly have it in the $828.43m consensus — but the pre-print wire copy does not. The 26 August previews (Benzinga, scanx) carry only '$0.09 vs $0.35 EPS' and '$828.43m revenue' and explicitly do not mention the extra week, FX, or the split-off. If the marginal holder had internalised that Q1 organic growth is mechanically ~15% rather than ~9%, you would expect a visible pre-print run-up rather than 20d +4.55% / 5d +0.15% at exactly the $20 IPO price, and you would not see two of five analysts (BofA $27->$20 on 18 May, Wells $26->$22 on 4 June) cutting targets into it. The first session is priced off the release headline, and the only prior print — a GAAP loss of $(0.68) that still produced +15.93% — is direct evidence this name trades off the growth line, not the EPS line.
evidence.independence: Corroborated independently by Medtronic's own FY27 guidance shape: Q1 FY27 non-GAAP EPS guided $1.38-1.40 (+~10% on Q1 FY26's $1.26) versus full-year growth of ~7%, which only reconciles if the 53rd week sits in Q1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1613103/000162828026040034/exhibit991-fy26q4earningsr.htm). Year-ago quarter-end date independently from the Medtronic Q1 FY26 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1613103/000161310325000161/mdt-20250725.htm

evidence.text: The euro tailwind that supplied roughly half of Q4 FY26's reported-vs-organic gap (15.6% reported vs 8.7% organic) is gone in this quarter: EURUSD monthly averages for May/Jun/Jul 2026 were 1.1681/1.1510/1.1419 (avg 1.1536) versus 1.1276/1.1518/1.1698 a year earlier (avg 1.1497) — +0.34% y/y, against +8.2% y/y for the Feb-Apr window that Q4 FY26 covered. MiniMed's 10-K puts OUS revenue at ~70% of FY26 total (Q4 FY26: international $599m of $837m, US only $238m), making it one of the most FX-levered US-listed medtechs.
evidence.why_not_priced: FX is the single most-modelled line on the sell side, so I size this small — most of it is in the $828m number. What is not priced is the interaction: the market's mental model of MMED is 'US insulin pump company with a new US pump', and a 70%-OUS revenue base whose reported growth has been running 7 points above organic on currency is not how a name trading at its IPO price with 833 contracts of total option open interest is being held. If it were understood, the reported-growth deceleration from a 7pt FX cushion to zero would have shown up as a pre-print de-rating rather than a 20d gain.
evidence.independence: Prior-year rates from the same publisher's 2025 page (https://www.x-rates.com/average/?from=EUR&to=USD&amount=1&year=2025); the 70% OUS figure is from a different document, MiniMed's FY26 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002062583/000162828026045915/mdt-20260424.htm

evidence.text: About $20m of Q4 FY26's $837m reported revenue was not product demand: the 'Other' line jumped to $22m from $2m a year earlier and the footnote defines it as 'net sales generated from the sales of smart insulin pens and services. Amounts in this line also reflect adjustments to the Company's Italian payback accruals' — a legal-accrual release that is expressly excluded from the organic growth definition. Anyone extrapolating the $837m base into Q1 has carried a one-off forward, and the underlying Italian exposure is live rather than settled: the Council of State (Ordinance No. 1589/2026) suspended industry appeals against the Ministry of Health decree of 29 December 2023 and referred the Medical Device Governance Fund to the Italian Constitutional Court.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a footnote to a supplementary revenue table in a press-release exhibit, not a headline item; no preview, initiation note summary or wire story I could find mentions the Italian payback at all. If it were priced, a $20m swing factor on a $830m quarter — 2.4 points of reported growth, sitting outside the organic definition and therefore invisible to anyone anchoring on 'organic' — would appear in preview commentary as a bridge item, and it does not. The sign is genuinely two-sided, which is why the band straddles zero.
evidence.independence: The Italian litigation status is from an entirely separate source chain: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/a-new-tax-on-medical-device-3576983/ (Hogan Lovells, on Council of State Ordinance No. 1589/2026 referring the Medical Device Governance Fund to the Constitutional Court)

evidence.text: The US business — the whole basis of the Flex equity story — grew 1.5% in Q4 FY26 ($238m of $837m) versus +12.2% organic internationally, and the reporting quarter cannot show the Flex inflection because Flex's actual differentiator arrived after quarter end: MiniMed's 2026-08-17 release says Flex 'now shipping' with Abbott's 15-day Instinct sensor, 17 days after the 2026-07-31 close, while the 2026-06-17 US launch release told customers the Instinct pairing was investigational and 'expected later in summer 2026'. The company therefore told prospective US pump buyers, inside the quarter, that a materially better bundle was weeks away.
evidence.why_not_priced: Coverage treats the 17 June US launch and the 17 August Instinct availability as two positive product headlines; nobody has joined them into 'the six weeks of Flex that land in this quarter were sold against a publicly pre-announced upgrade seventeen days out'. If the market had done that arithmetic, the 17 August release would have read as a mild negative revision to the reported quarter rather than as good news, and Flex-driven price targets would not still sit $20-26 against a $19.97 spot. The offset — and the reason this is only worth a point or so — is that the same fact makes Q2 commentary easy for management to spin.
evidence.independence: The 1.5% US growth and $238m US figure come from a different document, the Q4 FY26 earnings exhibit 99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2062583/000162828026040036/exhibit991-fy26q4earningsr.htm); the 'expected later in summer 2026' language is in the 2026-06-17 launch release, https://news.minimed.com/2026-06-17-MiniMeds-Smallest-App-Controlled-Insulin-Pump-is-Now-Available-in-the-U-S

evidence.text: Medtronic's April 2026 intrusion (ShinyHunters, unauthorised access 13-19 April 2026) resulted in notification of 3,834,294 individuals, with letters going out from late June into July 2026 — squarely inside MiniMed's fiscal Q1 — and several class actions already filed; exposed fields include Social Security numbers and health information. MiniMed filed its own Reg-FD 8-K on the incident on 2026-04-27 saying it was 'not aware of any compromises to the IT systems used by its business', but it has never quantified exposure, and the Q1 10-Q is the first periodic filing that must address it while MiniMed still runs on Medtronic IT under the separation arrangements.
evidence.why_not_priced: The breach is universally covered as a Medtronic story and was priced (to the extent it was priced at all) into MDT in late April; the diabetes business is the one Medtronic unit with millions of direct patient records (pumps, sensors, supply reordering), so MiniMed's share of the 3.8m is plausibly large, yet no MMED-specific coverage exists and MMED sits 3.5% off its 52-week high. If the market had attributed a material share of the remediation, indemnity and litigation exposure to MMED, you would see it in the pre-print tape and in a discount to the $20 IPO price, not a 20d gain.
evidence.independence: MiniMed's own Reg-FD 8-K on the incident, a separate primary source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2062583/000110465926049045/tm2612783d1_8k.htm

evidence.text: Informative absence on the largest feared mechanical event: as of 2026-08-31 neither Medtronic (CIK 0001613103) nor MiniMed (CIK 0002062583) has filed a Form S-4, Schedule TO or Form 425 for the split-off exchange offer, so an exchange offer cannot legally launch in the days around this print, and Medtronic's FY27 EPS guidance still 'assumes consolidation of the Diabetes business for the full 12 months of FY27'. Separation groundwork is visibly proceeding but at governance pace, not offer pace — the board went from 9 to 11 on 2026-06-29 adding Alcon CEO David Endicott as an independent director, and the first annual meeting is set for 2026-10-09.
evidence.why_not_priced: The received framing around any Medtronic carve-out is that the split-off exchange offer, launched at a discount, forces arbitrage shorting of a 28m-share float and caps the subsidiary — and the +22.1 vol-point 25-delta put skew is the kind of print that framing produces. The registration docket says that cannot happen in this window. This is worth little on its own, but it is the reason I do not read the skew as a directional statement, and confirming an absence at zero cost is the point.
evidence.independence: The full-12-month consolidation assumption is from a separate document, Medtronic's Q4 FY26 earnings exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1613103/000162828026040034/exhibit991-fy26q4earningsr.htm); the board expansion is from MiniMed's 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2062583/000110465926078588/tm2619270d1_8k.htm

evidence.text: Zepp set its H2 2026 margin expectations on 8 June 2026 with CFO Leon Deng naming memory as the specific gross-margin risk ("we expect higher memory costs to create near-term pressure on gross margins, driven by the industry-wide transition from DDR4 to DDR5 and high-bandwidth memory") and naming ASP increases plus a possible tariff refund as the offsets; since that date the consumer DRAM squeeze has escalated sharply — TrendForce on 22 June 2026 said consumer DRAM shortages had cascaded all the way down to DDR2 (contract prices +35-40% QoQ in 3Q26) and that OEMs/ODMs were substituting DDR4 designs with DDR3 and DDR3 with DDR2 to hold system cost. Zepp's gross margin had already fallen from a company-record 40.4% in Q4 2025 to 37.7% in Q1 2026, so the 1 September margin print and the H2 margin commentary are being made into a materially worse cost environment than the one management described in June.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody has a model to update. Nasdaq carries no EPS estimate and an n/a estimate count for ZEPP, the option chain is unusable (ATM bid-ask 109% of mid, 764 contracts total open interest, so there is no skew to read), and the stock is UP 12.98% over 20 sessions on ~38-41k shares a day. If a component-cost squeeze on a 37%-gross-margin hardware microcap were priced, you would see a pre-print drift lower, at least one preview note cutting a margin assumption, and puts bid; there is no coverage at all and no negative drift.
evidence.independence: Zepp's own transcript establishes the exposure (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/10/zepp-health-zepp-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/, 2026-06-10) and Tom's Hardware independently reports DRAM and NAND prices still climbing through Q3 2026 with consumers hitting an affordability limit (https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/ram/memory-price-surge-begins-to-cool-as-consumers-hit-affordability-limit-ai-demand-still-keeps-dram-and-nand-prices-climbing-through-q3-2026). TrendForce 2026-07-09 puts conventional DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 (https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20260709-13140.html).

evidence.text: The Balance 3 / Balance Ultra family, announced 2 June 2026 and presented as 'launched' in the Q1 release six days later, did not actually go on sale until the turn of June and July 2026 (Balance Ultra and Balance 3 Stainless Steel at the turn of the month, Balance 3 Titanium 'a few weeks later'). So the quarter being reported on 1 September carries essentially none of the new flagship line, while Q3 is the first quarter to carry both $599.99 SKUs (Balance Ultra and Cheetah 2 Ultra) — against a backdrop where portfolio ASPs rose more than 20% YoY in Q1 2026 and all seven 2026 launches were holding at MSRP with no discounting.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is product-press granularity that exists nowhere in a financial document: the Q1 press release and the wire copy say the products were launched, not that they shipped after quarter end. evidence.text: Rezolve has issued no new shares since the January 2026 raise (398.83m shares outstanding today = 336,327,587 at 31 Dec 2025 + the 62,500,000 sold at $4.00 on 21 Jan 2026, to the share), which lets H1 cash be bounded from the outside: $111.1m at 31 Dec 2025 + $250m gross January proceeds - $230m paid all-cash for Reward Loyalty on 10 Feb 2026 = at most ~$131m before H1 operating burn (FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was -$59m) and before the ~$102m Crownpeak/Monroe term loan that matures 31 Dec 2026 - so only a small single-digit-percent fraction of the $300m repurchase mandate is actually fundable, and the H1 balance sheet is where that arithmetic first becomes public.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no consensus balance sheet for this name: it is a semi-annual foreign private issuer with zero recoverable earnings-reaction history, five analysts all at Strong Buy with a $10.50 target, and every sell-side preview anchored on the pre-announced $127m revenue and the $360m guide. If the market had done this subtraction, the stock would not have run 16.8% in five days into the print on partnership press releases, front-expiry put/call open interest would not be 0.25, and the 30 June buyback mandate would not still be treated as a $300m bid. The share-count identity that makes the bound tight (zero issuance since January) is the piece nobody has cross-checked, and it is exactly what removes the 'they must have raised more' escape hatch.
evidence.independence: Cash of $111.1m at 31 Dec 2025 and adjusted EBITDA of -$59m come from the FY2025 results release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920294/000119312526130487/rzlv-ex99_1.htm, 2026-03-30); the 336,327,587 share count at 31 Dec 2025 from the 20-F (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/RZLV/20-f-rezolve-ai-plc-files-annual-report-foreign-issuer-7842680420d4.html, 2026-03-30, snippet_only for the exact figure); the $230m all-cash, 'no financing, no equity issuance' funding of Reward from https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/rezolve-ai-acquires-reward-loyalty-for-230-million-in-allcash-deal-93CH-4496476 (2026-02-13); the $250m at $4.00 from https://rezolve.com/press-releases/rezolve-ai-closes-250-million-oversubscribed-financing-enters-2026-with-one-of-the-strongest-balance-sheets-in-ai-commerce/ (2026-01-26).

evidence.text: The UK statutory accounts of Rezolve AI PLC (company 14573691) for the year ended 31 December 2025 were due at Companies House by 30 June 2026 and are still not filed as of 31 August 2026 - the register shows the last accounts on file as the period ending 31 December 2024 and flags accounts overdue - even though the company published an 'Annual Report and Accounts 2025' as Exhibit 99.2 to a 6-K on 30 March 2026, and its shareholders only passed the resolution covering auditor appointment on a resolution filed 22 July 2026, three weeks after the statutory deadline.
evidence.why_not_priced: No US aggregator, wire or terminal reads the UK register for a Nasdaq-listed issuer, and the company's own defence against Fuzzy Panda and Grizzly was explicitly that the shorts 'disregard audited financials'. If this were priced, the two published short theses would have led with it - a UK PLC two months delinquent on its statutory accounts while telling the market its audited numbers vindicate it is a free headline neither short has used, which is direct evidence it has not circulated. It matters into a print because the H1 figures are management-account based and unreviewed, and a delinquent statutory audit is the cheapest available reason to discount them.
evidence.independence: Corroborated within the same register by the 22 Jul 2026 'Resolutions' entry covering auditor appointment and share-purchase authority on the filing history page (https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/14573691/filing-history), and by the fact that the FY2025 accounts were already published to the SEC on 2026-03-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920294/000119312526130487/2025_results_pr_and_ar_6.htm), so the delay is not an absence of accounts.

evidence.text: Rezolve AI PLC - the listed parent itself, not a US subsidiary - registered a charge in favour of Monroe Capital Management Advisors LLC created 22 December 2025 and still outstanding, plus a second outstanding charge in favour of Crownpeak Technology Holdings LLC created 19 January 2026, meaning the ~$102m of Crownpeak term loans maturing 31 December 2026 (Term SOFR + 5.50%) are secured at the top of the group; the $300m buyback in turn requires a UK court-sanctioned capital reduction, expected mid-September, in which secured creditors get a formal creditor-protection say.
evidence.why_not_priced: The SEC disclosure frames the Monroe debt as loans 'assumed' with the acquired entity; the UK charges register is what shows the plc granted security over itself, and nothing in the US filing chain, the press releases or the two short reports mentions it. If the market had joined it to the capital reduction, the stock would not have rallied on the 30 June buyback mandate as if $300m were unconditional - the court route with a secured lender due to be repaid four months later is a live gate on both the timing and the size, and the 1 September call is the first place management has to speak to it after the mandate vote.
evidence.independence: The term-loan amount, 31 December 2026 maturity and the Monroe amended-and-restated credit agreement are established separately from the December 2025 6-K reproduction at https://www.streetinsider.com/SEC+Filings/Form+6-K+REZOLVE+AI+PLC+For:+Dec+01/25680399.html (2025-12-01, snippet_only); the mid-September court-approval condition is from the AGM release at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000119312526291046/rzlv-ex99_1.htm (2026-06-30). Partially overlaps finding 1 on the same debt maturity.

evidence.text: Rezolve took a $63.3m impairment in FY2025 on its SQD (Subsquid) token holdings and told investors continued volatility could force further impairments; SQD traded around a $0.0627 low in January 2026 and was capped by a $0.056-$0.058 resistance zone by June 2026, so the H1 2026 accounts most likely carry another digital-asset writedown into a net loss line the market has no estimate for, because only the revenue line was pre-announced.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 27 July pre-announcement gave revenue only and explicitly nothing on gross margin, EBITDA, cash or the bottom line, so there is no published loss estimate for H1 at all; a crypto token's H1 price path is not an input any RZLV preview contains. If this were priced you would see it discussed alongside the $127m headline rather than the ARR and partnership copy that has driven the last five sessions. I could not establish the residual carrying value of the token position after the 2025 writedown, which is why the band is wide and the point estimate small.
evidence.independence: SQD price levels are snippet_only from https://coinmarketcap.com/cmc-ai/subsquid/price-analysis/ (accessed 2026-08-31) and are a different source class entirely from the SEC disclosure of the impairment; independent of findings 1-3.

Reward Loyalty UK Limited (CH 10701520), the business Rezolve bought for $239,557,869 cash on 2026-02-10 and told US investors would add 'approximately $90 million of EBITDA-accretive revenue', filed audited group accounts at Companies House on 2026-07-25 for its year ended 30 April 2025 showing turnover of GBP 52.89m (approx $67-71m) and gross profit of about GBP 21m - i.e. a ~40% gross-margin business generating roughly GBP 2m EBITDA on 186-209 employees, not a 90%-margin software asset. [snippet_only: the 74-page PDF is behind an S3 redirect WebFetch cannot follow; figures are from two independent CH aggregators reading the same filing]
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the single largest component of Rezolve's revenue ramp and its real economics exist only in a UK private-company filing made five weeks ago, in GBP, on an April year-end, under a name no US screen maps to RZLV. If the market had it, the Feb 2026 deal would not have been sold to a US audience as 'non-dilutive' and 'EBITDA-accretive $90m revenue' without pushback, Cantor would not be carrying Overweight on a 90%-software-margin frame, and the front-expiry chain would not be 4:1 calls at a 0.25 put/call OI ratio. It also creates a two-sided trap on 1 September: consolidate Reward gross and consolidated gross margin collapses; consolidate net and the $360m guide loses ~$30m of its base.
evidence.independence: Independently corroborated by Endole reading the same 2026-07-25 filing (turnover GBP 52.89m, net assets GBP 5.99m, total liabilities GBP 57.83m, 209 employees) at https://open.endole.co.uk/insight/company/10701520-reward-loyalty-uk-limited . Cross-checks against finding 2 (the SEC-side gross-margin arithmetic) and against Rezolve's own $90m claim at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/02/10/3235266/0/en/Rezolve-Ai-PLC-Expands-Core-AI-Commerce-Platform-with-Acquisition-of-Reward-Loyalty-UK-Limited.html . The Companies House filing history establishing the 2026-07-25 group accounts (and that they were filed ~6 months past the 31 Jan 2026 statutory deadline) is at https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/10701520/filing-history

evidence.text: Rezolve's consolidated gross margin has already fallen from the 95.8% it reported for H1 2025 to 66.0% for audited FY2025 (revenue $46,800,099 less cost of revenue $15,922,202 per the 20-F income statement), which implies roughly 61% in H2 2025 - and H1 2026 is the FIRST period that consolidates Reward at all, on top of Crownpeak (from 1 Dec 2025) and GroupBy. The 1 September interims are the first gross-margin disclosure the market will see since the 95.8% print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody previews an FPI's semi-annual gross margin - there is no 10-Q, no quarterly cadence, and the baseline records n=0 recoverable earnings reactions on EDGAR, so there is no sell-side model of this line to be wrong about. The market's live anchor is the 95.8% H1 2025 figure, which was reported as a beat against a 60-70% analyst expectation, plus the company's own August 2026 assertion of 'core software margins above 90%' in its Commerce.com exchange-offer material. If a 40-point margin compression were priced, RZLV would not have added 16.8% in five sessions into the print and the 25-delta chain would show put demand rather than a 0.25 put/call OI ratio.
evidence.independence: The 95.8% H1 2025 gross margin and the 60-70% analyst expectation are from a separate source, the coverage of the H1 2025 interim 6-K, at https://www.investing.com/news/sec-filings/rezolve-ai-files-interim-financial-statements-for-first-half-of-2025-93CH-4267350 [snippet_only]. Mechanically this is the SEC-side confirmation of finding 1, reached from a different document set.

evidence.text: Both of Rezolve AI PLC's registered charges are still shown as OUTSTANDING at Companies House - Monroe Capital Management Advisors LLC (charge created 2025-12-22) and Crownpeak Technology Holdings LLC (created 2026-01-19) - covering the $101,540,086 Monroe borrowing that the 20-F classified as SHORT-TERM debt at 31 Dec 2025 and the $50,000,000 Crownpeak promissory notes, while no 6-K filed in 2026 announces any refinancing, and the 20-F's going-concern mitigation depended explicitly on 'refinancing short-term debt'. Cash arithmetic: $111,112,251 at 31 Dec 2025, plus the ~$250m registered direct raise closed 2026-01-21 (62.5m shares at $4, ~5% placement fee), less the $239,557,869 cash paid for Reward on 2026-02-10, leaves roughly $110m before any H1 operating burn (FY2025 operating burn was $63,147,255 on a far smaller cost base). The 1 September interims are the first balance sheet since 31 Dec 2025.
evidence.why_not_priced: Going concern is in the wire from the March 20-F, but the resolution of a $101.5m current maturity is not: the marginal holder has been given nine 6-Ks since June about India, a payments partner, the World Cup, watermarking, Google and Commerce.com, and not one about debt. The charge register is the only public place the security status is visible and it is a UK filing, not an SEC one. If the market had priced a cash-versus-current-debt squeeze, a 15%-of-float short base would not be facing a 0.25 put/call OI ratio and the stock would not have run 16.8% into a first-balance-sheet-in-eight-months event. The burn estimate is my arithmetic and flagged as such; the four dollar figures are each sourced.
evidence.independence: Debt composition and short/long split from the 20-F schedule at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920294/000119312526132456/R73.htm ; balance sheet at .../R2.htm ; FY2025 operating cash outflow at .../R8.htm ; the $239,557,869 Reward consideration and the 2026-01-20 issue of 62.5m shares at $4 at .../R111.htm ; the absence of any 2026 6-K on financing is verifiable from https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001920294.json

evidence.text: The entire +16.8% five-day run-up in the baseline is one company-issued press release: 'Google Selects Rezolve Ai's Proprietary Distributed Database Platform' on 2026-08-25, which moved the stock ~19% in a session (close 2.43 on 08-24, pre-market 2.645 on 08-25) and which discloses no contract value, no term, no revenue and no Google quote or spokesperson; Google's own Blockchain Analytics / Web3 documentation and partner blogs name Subsquid and Chainstack for exactly this function and do not mention Rezolve; and Rezolve did not furnish the release on a Form 6-K, its last 6-K being 2026-08-06.
evidence.why_not_priced: The market has priced this as a hard commercial win - a 19% single-session repricing of a $1.1bn market cap is ~$210m of value ascribed to an announcement carrying zero disclosed economics. The 1 September call is the first forum where management must either quantify it inside the $360m guide or decline to. The sweep's brief attributes the run-up to the 2026-08-06 revenue pre-announcement, which is arithmetically impossible for a five-day window, so even the baseline's own reading of what is priced is wrong here. Note the immediately prior promotional release (2026-08-18, World Cup scale metrics) drew a -5.94% reaction, which is the fade pattern this name actually has.
evidence.independence: Google-side absence checked directly against Google's own documentation at https://docs.cloud.google.com/blockchain-analytics/docs/supported-datasets and the Google Cloud Web3 partner posts; the day-by-day price path and the 08-18 reaction are from a different source at https://stockstotrade.com/news/rezolve-ai-plc-rzlv-news-2026_08_25/ . Independent of findings 1-3, which are accounting rather than narrative.

evidence.text: The reaffirmed ~$360m FY2026 guide requires H2 2026 revenue of ~$233m against ~$127m in H1, +83% half-on-half, at a point where the acquired run-rates are largely already in the base: Reward at GBP 52.89m/yr (~$67-71m), Crownpeak at ~$70m/yr for an $81.0m purchase price, GroupBy at ~$30m/yr - about $84m per half combined - leaving roughly $149m of H2 from everything else versus roughly $43m in H1.
evidence.why_not_priced: The halves arithmetic ($127m and $360m) is derivable from the 2026-08-06 wire and I assume it is priced; the part that is not is the acquired-revenue denominator, which needs Reward's actual GBP turnover from a Companies House filing rather than the $90m the US market was given. I am sizing this small precisely because most of it IS in the wire - it is a decomposition, not a discovery, and it earns a small number.

evidence.text: BizLink (3665.TW), named in Credo's FY2026 10-K as the third-party manufacturer of its AEC products, printed accelerating record monthly revenue straight through Credo's fiscal Q1 (3 May - 1 Aug 2026): May NT$7.352bn (-0.4% MoM, +41.3% YoY), June NT$8.518bn (+15.9% MoM, +63.8% YoY), July NT$9.630bn (+13.1% MoM, +59.6% YoY, all-time high) — roughly +31% across the May-to-July span against a Credo revenue guide implying only +6.4% to +8.7% sequential.
evidence.why_not_priced: Taiwan-exchange monthly revenue filings are not carried in any US sell-side preview of CRDO — the Zacks, Seeking Alpha and Investing.com previews all frame the quarter off the company's own $465-475m guide and the ~$471.7m consensus with no channel data at all. If the market had made this read, the front-expiry 25-delta skew would not sit at +7.31 vol points to the put side, and the stock would not have surrendered the entire $283-to-$216 August move into a print whose sole named AEC manufacturer was printing back-to-back record months. The BizLink July figure is dated 5 August 2026 (year confirmed in the technews.tw URL path /2026/08/05/), i.e. after Credo last spoke on 1 June and inside the quarter being reported.
evidence.independence: Three independent post-1-June datapoints point the same way, none of them Credo's and none sharing a document with each other or with BizLink: Amphenol's Q2 2026 (29 July) IT datacom sales +89% reported / +63% organic with company book-to-bill 1.23:1 (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/APH/amphenol-reports-record-second-quarter-2026-4qu1ti0ylasq.html); Fabrinet's FQ4 2026 (17 August) datacenter revenue $669m, +68% YoY, with FQ1 guided to $1.375-1.425bn (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/17/3346479/0/en/fabrinet-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results.html); and Marvell's FQ2 2027 (27 August) beat with FY27 and FY28 revenue outlooks both raised (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260827816134/en/Marvell-Technology-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2027-Financial-Results). The BizLink-manufactures-Credo's-AECs link is verified in the 10-K itself: 'BizLink Technology, Inc. (BizLink) for manufacturing our AEC products' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001807794/000162828026043303/crdo-20260502.htm).

evidence.text: Credo filed no Item 2.02 8-K — indeed no 8-K of any kind — between 1 June and 1 September 2026, even though this quarter has the same ~31-day quarter-end-to-print gap (ended 1 Aug, prints 1 Sep) as fiscal Q3 2026 (ended 31 Jan, printed 2 Mar), when on 9 February 2026 it pre-announced preliminary revenue of $404-408m against prior guidance of $335-345m nine days after quarter end.
evidence.why_not_priced: No aggregator publishes the fact that a company did not file. The EDGAR 8-K list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001807794&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=20) shows the last 8-K as 2026-06-01, so under an identical calendar structure the company chose silence where it once chose to disclose a ~19%-above-guide quarter. That thins the fat right tail. If the market had drawn this inference, front-month ATM IV would not be 140.7% and the three-day straddle would not be pricing an 11.73% move; the option market is still paying for a Feb-9-style shock in either direction.
evidence.independence: none — this is an absence-of-filing inference and nothing independently corroborates a negative reading of it. It is deliberately sized small and asymmetric for that reason.

evidence.text: Both mechanisms that could crash this print were pre-committed by management on the 1 June call: the CFO guided Q2 FY27 sequential growth as 'mid single digits, between our Q1 guide, and you can expect something similar in our Q2 guide' (i.e. roughly $490-500m), and guided FY27 non-GAAP gross margin 'to be broadly consistent with fiscal year 2026 levels' — whereas the -14.81% reaction on 2 March 2026 was caused specifically by cutting the Q4 non-GAAP gross-margin guide to 64-66% from 68.6% reported, not by revenue.
evidence.why_not_priced: The previews in circulation (Seeking Alpha's '$600M optical revenue ramp in focus', Zacks' 'CRDO Bets on Optical Boom to Drive 80%+ Growth') frame the story as an H2 hockey stick and never state that the Q2 number is already pre-guided to mid-single-digit sequential — so a Q2 guide near $495m, which screens as a violent deceleration off 108-113% YoY growth, carries no new information. If the market had priced that, the 25-delta skew would not be +7.31 vol points put-side on a name whose put/call open interest ratio is only 0.81 and which has already round-tripped -24% from its 18 August level; the skew is paying for a guidance shock whose shape and margin floor were both put on the record three months ago.
evidence.independence: Corroborated from a different document that the March crash was a margin event, not a revenue event: the 2 March 2026 print beat on both lines ($407m revenue, $1.07 non-GAAP EPS vs $0.94 consensus) and still fell, with the Q4 non-GAAP GM guide of 64-66% named as the cause (https://www.alphaspread.com/market-news/earnings/credo-posts-strong-q3-fiscal-2026-results-revenue-soars-but-stock-falls). Note this finding shares the 1 June transcript with nothing else in this file, but it and finding 2 are two different readings of the same broad thesis — that the realised move should land inside the 9.6% implied — and should be collapsed if the scorer treats that as one claim.

evidence.text: Both of Dell's closest server-assembler comparables reported the overlapping April-June 2026 quarter in mid-August with massive margin upside in the teeth of the memory spike - Super Micro delivered 17.5% GAAP gross margin on 11 Aug against its own prior guidance of 8.2-8.4%, and Lenovo's ISG posted a record 9.1% operating margin on 13 Aug against a ~4.6% consensus - which is the direct empirical refutation of the 'the assembler eats the memory bill' thesis that Dell's own preview coverage says is the whole question for this print.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 31 Aug Motley Fool preview - the piece that defines the sell-side framing for this print, and which explicitly makes ISG operating margin versus Q1's 10.5% the pass/fail test - names no comparable at all, saying only that 'chip designers have spent recent weeks describing what those costs are doing to their margins'. If the comps' actual margin outcome were in the price, DELL would not be 10.8% off its 52-week high with a -5.58% 20-day run-up, Morgan Stanley would not be Equal-Weight at $434 and UBS Neutral at $455 against a $441.19 spot, and the stock would not have handed back the whole +10% it made on 13 Aug plus more over the following two weeks. The market saw this datapoint once and then un-priced it; the sell-side never wrote it down as a Dell read-across at all.
evidence.independence: Lenovo's own primary release is a separate company and a separate document: https://www.techpowerup.com/351574/lenovo-reports-record-usd-26-9b-revenue-for-q1-2026-27 (2026-08-13, ISG revenue $8.5bn +98%, operating profit $777m, 9.1% margin, all-time high). The 4.63% consensus comparison comes from a third source, https://finance.biggo.com/news/5207dece-281c-490c-a9fa-040c66945089. Note these two are separate filings from separate issuers, not two readings of one document - but they share one mechanism (component-cost pass-through by assemblers), so they should be collapsed with finding 2 to the extent that mechanism is the thing being priced.

evidence.text: IDC's calendar-Q2 2026 PC data, covering two of the three months of Dell's fiscal Q2, shows the memory shortage working as a pricing-power event rather than a margin event for OEMs - shipments fell 4.9% to 68.2m units and Dell fell 5% to 9.3m while industry revenue rose, with comparable-line prices up 20-40% year over year and IDC stating vendors 'are pushing through price increases faster than demand is dropping'; Dell held share at 13.6%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The entire preview conversation on DELL is about ISG; CSG is roughly a third of revenue and is where memory inflation is proportionally most severe against a mid-single-digit segment margin, so a CSG print is the leg with the most room to surprise in either direction. The visible tell that it is unpriced is that the headline the market consumed from this data was 'PC shipments fall for the first time in two years' and 'Dell -5%', not the revenue and ASP mechanic underneath it - and Dell's own Q1 FY27 already showed CSG operating margin going the opposite way to the fear, up 280bp year over year to 8.0% (three months ended 1 May 2026, 10-Q). If the market had joined those two facts, the run-up into this print would not be negative and the coverage would be arguing about CSG, which it is not.
evidence.independence: Dell's own segment disclosure, a different document and a different issuer-period: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001571996/000157199626000030/dell-20260501.htm (CSG operating income $1,170m, 8.0% of segment revenue, up 280bp). Jeff Clarke's 28 May statement that Dell is 'repricing it feels like every day' is the stated mechanism: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/dell-dell-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/. Shares the pass-through mechanism with finding 1 - collapse the pair if scoring by mechanism rather than by document.

evidence.text: FuelCell's own careers site right now shows 61 of its 80 open requisitions at the Torrington cell plant and, critically, an entire third shift being staffed end-to-end -- Supervisor Tape Casting (Third Shift), Sheet Metal Supervisor (Third Shift), Warehouse Supervisor (Third Shift), Material Handler (Third Shift), QA Inspector Manufacturing (Third Shift), EH&S Specialist (Third Shift), Facility Tech (Third Shift), Janitor (Third Shift) and Security Officer (3rd Shift), plus a parallel second-shift set -- i.e. a 24/7 line being commissioned, not incremental backfill.
evidence.why_not_priced: Management explicitly declined to give a current annualised production rate on the 8 June call, so the only public number is the aspiration (500 MW/yr, $200-275m, 24 months). Nobody aggregates shift designations in job postings. If the market had this, the mid-August coverage would be arguing about output cadence and the $213m raise as pre-funded plant capex; instead the wire copy is 'dilution concerns tied to the $225m July offering' and rate-driven risk-off, and 25-delta puts would not be bid 11.6 vol points over calls on a name whose plant is hiring janitors and security guards for a third shift. evidence.text: Homer John Livingston III, who only became a FuelCell director on 19 May 2026, bought 26,343 shares in the open market on 16 July 2026 at a weighted-average $18.79 (about $495k, transaction code P, direct) -- an actual cash purchase at a company where every other recent insider line is a director-fee stock grant or a 10b5-1 sale.
evidence.why_not_priced: It was filed on 20 July into the middle of the sector de-rating and the stock has fallen another 11% since, so it plainly did not set the price; a market that had weighted it would not be paying an 11.6-point put skew nine days before the print. The signal is the contrast, and the contrast requires reading three separate accessions in the same week rather than a headline: the two Form 4s filed 16 July are zero-price director-fee deferred stock units (Livingston 833 units, Hansen 988 units) and the 6 July Form 4 is an EVP selling 2,500 shares at $28.71 under a plan adopted in January. Instead upside is the expensive side, so the tail that PANW confirms a Cribl/ClickHouse-scale deal tonight is effectively unhedged. evidence.text: Tonight's first-ever FY27 EPS guide has to be built on roughly 9-10% more shares than the FY26 base: PANW's own Q3 FY26 release guides FY26 diluted shares to 763-766m but Q4 alone to 830-840m, and PANW has already cut its own FY26 EPS guide once on this exact mechanism (from $3.80-3.90 to $3.65-3.70 on 17 Feb 2026, on deal costs that more than doubled), a print after which the stock closed -6.82%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q4 number cannot surprise: published consensus IS the company's guide (Q4 revenue $3,352m vs guide $3,345-3,355m; EPS $0.97 vs guide $0.96-0.98; shares 830-840m identical to the guide). If the market had priced the denominator step-up and this management's demonstrated willingness to guide EPS down on integration costs, you would not see a -17.1 skew with calls bid, and previews would be leading on FY27 EPS rather than on NGS ARR and platformization. The 17 Feb 2026 episode is the proof of concept: a double beat, an EPS guide cut, -6.82% the next day.

evidence.text: PANW's GSA OneGov agreement gives every federal agency up to 60% off list on designated bundles of Prisma AIRS Runtime Security, VM-Series software firewalls, Panorama/CDSS, Prisma SASE and Prisma Browser (35% on Code to Cloud) through 31 Jan 2028 - and PANW's fiscal Q1 FY27, the quarter it guides tonight, is the first US federal year-end (30 Sep) buying quarter to run entirely under that pricing.

If the market had priced it, the sell-side previews would carry a federal price-realisation line - the two previews I read (Hudson Labs 10 Aug, the 30 Aug Barchart/Yahoo piece) discuss only NGS ARR, RPO, platformization and organic growth, and neither mentions federal pricing at all. evidence.text: The Strait of Hormuz shipping crisis worsened sharply during Quanex's exact Q3 window (May-July 2026) - the conflict resumed in July and transits collapsed to roughly 5% of pre-war levels by August - directly undermining the 'rate of inflationary pressure subsides' assumption that management baked into the Q3 revenue/margin outlook when they gave it on June 4.
evidence.why_not_priced: The name carries only one published estimate, so Q3 segment margins are effectively unmodelled by the street, and every US-housing-starts screen that covers this stock treats it as a domestic R&R/new-construction demand story and misses the international logistics cost line entirely. If the market had focused on this, the near-flat-YoY consensus EPS would have been cut, the option skew would not be null, and the run-up would be worse than -10%. Management themselves flagged on the Q2 call that Hormuz-driven transportation and raw-material costs and expensive GCC re-routing hit the quarter ending April 30 - and the situation got materially worse, not better, after that.
evidence.independence: Quanex's own Q2 2026 earnings call independently confirms the mechanism and their exposure: 'Getting product through the Straits of Hormuz is not feasible at this point... significantly more expensive' logistics chains, and 'a significant increase in transportation and raw material costs during the quarter' - https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/05/quanex-nx-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

evidence.text: Quanex's leverage cushion is thin (3.1x net-debt/LTM-EBITDA at 4/30/26 against a 3.25x covenant that tightened from 3.75x this fiscal year), and the strong Q3 2025 quarter ($70.3M adj EBITDA) rolls OUT of the LTM denominator this print while Q3 2026 price-cost recovery is by management's own account incomplete until Q4 - so the ratio can tick UP toward the covenant in Q3 before the Q4 improvement they are guiding to.
evidence.why_not_priced: The covenant step-down to 3.25x and the roll-off of a strong comp is arithmetic buried in the credit-agreement footnote and the LTM bridge; with one analyst covering the name, nobody is publicly modelling the quarter-by-quarter leverage path, so a Q3 ratio that brushes 3.2x-plus would be a surprise the flat-YoY consensus does not contemplate. If priced, the put skew would be positive (it is null) and puts would be bid rather than the chain being near-dead at 199 total OI.
evidence.independence: Same directional thesis as finding 1 (weaker-than-consensus Q3 margins) but rests on a different document - the Q2 press release covenant/LTM disclosure rather than external Hormuz data - and the covenant math is the transmission mechanism that makes a margin miss matter more to the equity here than for an unlevered peer; management's stated intent to 'exit 2026 with a lower net leverage ratio' is explicitly a Q4 story, per https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/05/quanex-nx-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/
