evidence.text: The EU 21st-package carve-out that drove DLNG from $3.32 (16 July) to $3.85 (23 July) is a third-country-deliveries-only derogation expiring 25 July 2027, renewable one year at a time by Council vote and capped at the operator's 2025 volumes; the AIS work identifying the Dynagas vessels it protects names Clean Planet, Clean Vision, Clean Ocean and Clean Horizon - none of which are among the listed partnership's six ships - while DLNG's own Yamal-chartered Lena River last called at Huelva, Spain, an EU import terminal, departing 25 August 2026, i.e. exactly the EU-delivery employment the derogation does not cover.
evidence.why_not_priced: Dynagas holds no earnings call and has said nothing in writing since 29 May 2026, when its 6-K still stated that losing the Yamal charters 'would have a material adverse effect' and that it was studying 'the feasibility of lawfully removing the E.U. nexus'; the 8 September release is the first company text after the derogation. If the market had read the derogation's terms rather than the headline it would not have paid +9.17% and +4.34% on 22-23 July and then held most of it - and a $135m MLP with no analyst coverage, no EPS estimate and 41 contracts of total option open interest has no mechanism through which anyone reconciled the Official Journal text with which four hulls actually sit inside the listed entity. Coverage, if this were priced, would look like a note distinguishing the sponsor's Arc7 fleet from the MLP's 1A fleet; no such note exists.
evidence.independence: Two separate documents reach the same reading of the text independently of the urgewald analysis: euobserver, 27 July 2026, states the exemption covers LNG 'to third countries' and explicitly not European deliveries (https://euobserver.com/230246/brussels-found-russias-lng-weak-spot-then-carved-out-an-exception-for-a-greek-billionaire/), and High North News, 4 August 2026, gives the 25 July 2027 expiry, the annual Council renewal and the 2025 volume cap (https://en.highnorthnews.com/politics/eu-softens-russian-lng-sanctions-allowing-shipping-and-trading-to-continue-beyond-2027/1115356). The fleet-identity leg is independently checkable against the partnership's own Q1 6-K, which lists its six vessels as Clean Energy, Ob River, Amur River, Arctic Aurora, Yenisei River and Lena River (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm). NOTE ON CLUSTERING: the vessel-identity leg and the destination-split leg both come out of the same urgewald document, so treat them as one source, not two.

evidence.text: Clean Energy, the vessel DLNG moved onto a Rio Grande LNG charter 'at higher daily rates' at the end of April 2026, has sat at anchor in Southeast Asia in ballast (draught 8.9 m, speed 0.1 knots) with no destination and no ETA since departing Singapore Anchorage on 5 August 2026 - 33 days idle - while Arctic Aurora, still trading normally (loaded at Melkoya, Norway on 7 September for Klaipeda), is contracted to begin a second seven-year Rio Grande charter between September and November 2026, which would put a third of the six-ship fleet on hire to a project company whose Brownsville trains are not yet producing.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates AIS for a 50k-ADV MLP. This does not touch Q2 revenue - Q2 ended 30 June and time-charter hire is paid whether the ship moves or not - so the channel is the presentation's fleet-employment page and any disclosure of sublet or restructured arrangements with Rio Grande LNG, LLC, plus the Arctic Aurora delivery window. Had the market focused on it, a name whose entire equity story is charter counterparty quality would carry commentary on a pre-operational charterer holding two of six hulls; there is none, and the July rally treated the charter book as de-risked rather than concentrated. I am deliberately sizing this small because the contractual cash flow is unaffected.
evidence.independence: Two other vessels checked the same day on separate pages show the idling is not fleet-wide, which is what makes the Clean Energy datum interpretable rather than a data artefact: Ob River is en route Anjeong, Korea (departed 5 September) to Zhuhai, China (https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9315692), and Arctic Aurora departed Melkoya, Norway on 7 September at 18.3 knots for Klaipeda (https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9645970). Separately, the partnership's Q1 6-K is the source for the end-April Rio Grande delivery and the 'higher daily rates' characterisation (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm).

evidence.text: Six directors of Dynagas LNG Partners filed initial Section 16 ownership statements on 18 and 30 March 2026, every one of them carrying event date 18 March 2026 - George Prokopiou reporting 15,595,000 common units and 35,526 GP units indirectly through Dynagas Holding Ltd (50.4% beneficial interest), Alexios Rodopoulos 500 units direct, Dimitrios Anagnostopoulos 'no securities owned' - even though the partnership is exempt from Section 16 as a foreign private issuer under Rule 3a12-3(b), filed a 20-F for FY2025 on 8 April 2026 and has continued filing 6-Ks rather than 10-Qs through 13 August 2026; no Form 4 has followed in the five and a half months since.
evidence.why_not_priced: I am filing this at zero because I could not resolve it, not because it is unimportant: it is a genuine contradiction in the filing record that I can document and cannot explain. A board that becomes Section 16 reporting normally means the issuer has concluded it no longer qualifies as a foreign private issuer, which would force 10-Q/10-K/8-K, US-GAAP-only reporting and proxy statements - or it is the compliance footprint of a transaction. Neither has surfaced. If the market had noticed, a $135m MLP would show speculation about domestic-filer conversion or a going-private, and the 8 September event would not be scheduled as a 6-K with no conference call. I refuse to guess a sign, so it carries no directional weight; the band is width, not a view.
evidence.independence: none - the only corroboration is that the same EDGAR submissions index shows both the Form 3 cluster and the continuing 6-K/20-F pattern, which is the same source (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001578453.json), and no press, filing or company statement anywhere explains the 18 March 2026 event date.

evidence.text: Charter expiry cliff - the door the sweep pointed at - is closed: Yenisei River to Yamal Trade 2033, Lena River 2034, Clean Energy to Rio Grande from April 2026, Arctic Aurora to Rio Grande for ~7 years from Sept-Nov 2026, Ob River and Amur River to SEFE to 2028. Nothing rolls off in 2026-27 that is not already contracted forward, and coverage is 100%/100%/65% for 2026/27/28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000131786126000029/f052926dlng6k.htm).

Distribution catalyst - there is none. The Q2 common distribution of $0.050 was already declared on 13 August 2026 and the Series A preferred distribution of $0.5625 (44th consecutive) on 23 July 2026, so the 8 September release carries no capital-return news (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/13/3344926/0/en/dynagas-lng-partners-lp-announces-cash-distribution-for-the-quarter-ended-june-30-2026-of-0-050-per-common-unit.html).

Late-report signal - none. DLNG has always reported Q2 in early September; Q2 2025 was released before the open on 8 September 2025, so 8 September 2026 is exactly on cadence, not a delay (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/03/3144042/0/en/Dynagas-LNG-Partners-LP-Announces-Date-for-the-Release-of-the-Second-Quarter-and-Six-Month-2025-Results.html).

The Fayard drydock story - the six Arc7 hulls named as booked into Denmark's Fayard yard in summer 2026 before the January 2027 EU maritime-services ban are Rudolf Samoylovich, Georgiy Brusilov, Boris Davydov, Vladimir Vize, Nikolay Zubov and Nikolay Yevgenov. None is a DLNG vessel, so the off-hire angle does not reach the MLP (https://www.urgewald.org/en/media/danish-shipyard-receives-first-six-russia-linked-arctic-lng-tankers-eu-maritime, 2026-07-02).

Sponsor take-private or unit accumulation - no SC 13D and no SC 13D/A has been filed since 2017 and there has been no Form 4 ever. The only 2026 ownership filing is a passive SCHEDULE 13G by an individual, Thomas W. Herfort, for 1,901,981 units (5.17%), event date 4 August 2026, filed 11 August 2026 - real flow at ~38x average daily volume, but it is on EDGAR and was written up by aggregators, so I treat it as thinly priced rather than unpriced and give it no weight (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1578453/000119983526000285/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml).

Refinancing - the four sale-and-leaseback facilities with China Development Bank Financial Leasing (Clean Energy $38.6m, Ob River $51.2m, Amur River $52.7m ~3 years each, Arctic Aurora $125.2m ~9 years, $266.2m total) amortise rather than balloon, $11.0m repaid in Q1 2026, so there is no maturity wall for a refinancing announcement to clear.

The company's own website (dynagaspartners.com, including the /upload_press/ PDF path and the Presentations page) returned HTTP 503 on every attempt on 2026-09-07, and the Wayback API has no snapshot of the presentations page, so I could not front-run the slide deck or diff the fleet table on the company's own pages.

Yamal-side operational distress that would reach DLNG's P&L - Bellona's AIS-derived monthly Arctic report for May 2026 counts 25 Sabetta cargoes to Belgium, France, the Netherlands and Spain and names no Dynagas vessel; and because both Yamal ships are on time charter to 2033/2034, the fact that Yenisei River was drifting at 1.9 knots off southwest Ireland and Lena River was steaming 'FOR ORDERS' on 6-7 September 2026 costs the partnership no hire (https://etc.bellona.org/2026/07/09/monthly-highlights-from-the-russian-arctic-may-2026/, https://www.vesselfinder.com/vessels/details/9629598).

A quantifiable Q2 revenue surprise - the arithmetic is already public and roughly offsetting: Q1 2026 carried off-hire from unscheduled repairs on two vessels (95.1% utilisation vs 98.8% in Q4 2025) which should not repeat, against roughly three weeks of Clean Energy redelivery gap in April 2026 inside Q2. Q1 revenue was $39.9m and adjusted EBITDA $24.3m; I have no basis to call Q2 materially away from that.

evidence.text: July 2026 was the warmest month in the entire 131-year contiguous-US temperature record (76.9degF, all 48 states above their 20th-century average, none near or below normal) and it is the final and seasonally largest month of ServiceTitan's fiscal Q2, which ended 31 July 2026 - record cooling load is the direct driver of the emergency HVAC service calls and same-day replacement tickets that flow through Gross Transaction Volume and the payments take-rate, i.e. the ~25% of revenue that is variable ($66.8m of the $268.8m reported in Q1 was non-subscription).
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody cross-reads NOAA NCEI into a vertical-SaaS name, and the coverage proves it: the 4-Sep-2026 preview of this print says the two metrics that will define the quarter are subscription revenue growth and margin progress, and treats trades demand only as a qualitative risk ('when demand in those trades cools, there is no other segment to absorb the impact'). If the record heat were priced there would be at least one published note tying GTV to July cooling degree days, GTV would be the named metric to watch instead of subscription revenue, and the front-month skew would not be paying 5.14 vol points for downside on a stock that just fell 13.66% in five sessions. GTV and take-rate are disclosed only in the release, so there is no interim print to have arbitraged this away.
evidence.independence: AHRI industry shipments for June 2026 rose 21.7% y/y (central AC +26.8%, heat pumps +15.1%), the same physical demand pulse from a completely separate source - https://refindustry.com/news/ahri-reports-21-7-rise-in-u-s-ac-and-heat-pump-shipments/ (2026-08-19). Note this is the same THESIS as finding 3 below (end market did not cool) but rests on a different series and a different revenue line than finding 2.

evidence.text: ServiceTitan bills roughly $245-400 per technician per month, so its subscription line is mechanically a function of how many technicians its contractors employ - and BLS JOLTS shows construction hires in July 2026, the last month of ServiceTitan's fiscal Q2, at 366,000, up 14.7% month-over-month and 9.9% year-over-year, the highest construction hiring rate in about two years, with openings at 326,000 (+9.4% m/m).
evidence.why_not_priced: The JOLTS release landed 2026-09-02, six days before the print, into a five-day window in which the stock fell 13.66% - so the tape moved hard the other way after the datapoint existed, which is what unpriced looks like. The seat-count-to-JOLTS link is also not in any coverage: the pricing model is per-technician but ServiceTitan does not disclose seats, so the sell-side models net dollar retention as a black box rather than as trades headcount. If this were priced, the >110% NDR line would be treated as de-risked rather than as the swing factor, and the 25-delta skew would not be paying for downside.
evidence.independence: The BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 (released 2026-09-04) shows construction +22,000 with nonresidential specialty trade contractors +8,000, and ENR reports residential specialty trade contractors added 3,400 in August - a second government series, one month later, still positive: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_09042026.htm and https://www.enr.com/articles/63625-in-august-specialty-trade-contractors-again-led-construction-industrys-hiring . Different mechanism and different revenue line from finding 1 (seats/subscription vs GTV/payments), same overall thesis.

evidence.text: The visible HVAC datapoint an analyst would cross-read into ServiceTitan is Lennox's 30-July print - residential revenue -7%, unit volume -12%, full-year growth guide cut from ~4% to ~1% - but that is a company-specific channel and share story (Lennox's own one-step volumes fell mid-teens, new construction -30%), while the industry-wide series over the same window went the other way: Watsco, the largest US HVAC distributor, reported domestic residential HVAC equipment sales +5% with unit volume +2% and ASPs +2% and titled its release 'further industry stabilization'; Lennox's own CEO said the repair-versus-replace trend 'has stabilized', and a repair-skewed market with record heat maximises job count and technician demand, which is what ServiceTitan monetises rather than equipment units.
evidence.why_not_priced: TTAN carries only ~5 revenue estimates on an ~$8bn company, and the March-to-July wave of price-target cuts (Goldman $117 to $84, Citi $117 to $88, Truist $130 to $100, Canaccord $140 to $105, BTIG $130 to $105) was framed on multiple derating and AI cost, not on a reconciliation of Lennox against Watsco and AHRI. If the market had reconciled them, the residual bear case on TTAN would be purely the AI-seat-cannibalisation argument and the -29% drawdown from the 52-week high would not still be accompanied by a paid-for downside skew. Watsco's own stock fell ~15% on this release for a gross-margin reason, which buried the demand line inside it.
evidence.independence: Lennox's own commentary is the counterparty to this finding rather than support for it - https://homepros.news/lennox-posts-12-drop-in-residential-unit-volume-cuts-full-year-outlook/ (2026-07-30). Same thesis as finding 1; treat the NOAA/AHRI/Watsco/Lennox cluster as one end-market cluster, not three.

evidence.text: No S-1/S-3 resale registration, no announced secondary or follow-on offering, and no 8-K of any kind on EDGAR since 2026-08-01 - the only recent filings are routine Form 4s (CFO Dave Sherry sold at $90.02-92.01 on 2026-08-13/17), Form 144s dated 2026-08-04/11/12/14, a CEO intent-to-sell of 35,000 shares (~3.3% of his direct holding) filed 2026-08-04, and two Schedule 13G/13G/A filings. Insider supply is routine 10b5-1 distribution, small versus a 65.3m float, and fully visible in EDGAR, so it is priced.

ServiceTitan's own status page shows no incidents, 99.98% site and 100% mobile/core-feature uptime over the trailing 90 days - i.e. no peak-season outage to drive a churn or contractor-rage story either way.

No acquisition announced during fiscal Q2 FY27. The Convex, Conduit Tech and Schedule Engine deals surfacing in search are 2025 announcements (GlobeNewswire URL path /2025/09/18/) that closed in fiscal Q3 FY2026 - a relabelled-date trap I discarded.

The 'Carrier residential volumes down over 40%' figure that search served as current is Carrier's Q3/Q4 2025, not 2026 - discarded on date, and it would have inverted the finding had I used it. Likewise a widely-served 'YTD through July down 3.5% to 2,773,432 units' AHRI figure is the July 2025 release, not 2026.

Hiring-page teardown was inconclusive: ~11 pages of listings on servicetitan.com/careers, 62 US roles on Glassdoor, and no visible surge or deletion of a Max/AI onboarding team despite management naming onboarding capacity as the binding constraint on doubling Max locations again in Q2. One Enterprise Implementation Consultant listing was removed 2026-05-27; a single removal is not a team deletion and I dropped it.

Contractor-side churn evidence (Reddit price-hike threads, BBB data-export complaints, ServiceTitan-alternative comparison pages) is entirely SEO content-farm material with no dateable primary anchor, and price-increase grievances against ServiceTitan are perennial rather than new to this quarter.
Revelio Labs headcount data (3,529 employees, 444 postings) is only current through March 2026 - too stale to say anything about the May-July quarter.

No investor-conference appearance or intra-quarter management commentary between the 2026-06-04 Q1 call and today; last year's Pantheon investor session was 2025-09-18, so the 2026 user conference falls after this print.

Short interest is public and therefore priced: 7.25m shares, 7.60% of shares outstanding, 11.12% of float, 5.26 days to cover as of 2026-09-08, DOWN from 9.57m the prior month (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ttan/statistics/). I used it only to haircut my magnitude, not as a finding.

evidence.text: BLS PPI for 'Plastics Sewer, Stormdrain and Water Main Pipe' (WPU072106038) — CNM's single largest product exposure — averaged 185.2 across May/Jun/Jul 2026 (CNM's fiscal Q2, 4 May-2 Aug) versus 186.5 a year earlier, i.e. -0.7% y/y, against -8.2% y/y in CNM's fiscal Q1 (Feb-Apr 2026: 174.95 vs 190.48); the July 2026 reading of 188.565 is actually +1.9% ABOVE July 2025 and +8.2% above the March 2026 trough, so the deflation that drove the Sept-2025 guidance cut had fully reversed by the last month of this quarter.
evidence.source_date: 2026-07-01 (latest monthly observation; series pulled 2026-09-08 via fredgraph.csv?id=WPU072106038)
evidence.why_not_priced: On 10 June management told investors the opposite shape: Robyn Bradbury said 'PVC will still be down year over year even if we do get some uplift' and put the majority of the pricing impact in Q3, and the sell-side preview narrative into tomorrow is still PVC deflation. Nobody re-cuts a BLS six-digit commodity index onto a 4-May-to-2-August fiscal quarter. If the market had done it, CNM would not have printed a new 52-week low at $41.87 on 3 September, 25-delta puts would not be bid 3.24 vol points over calls, and Northcoast would not have cut to neutral on 26 August. The mechanism matters twice: it lifts Q2 revenue mix and, more importantly, it underwrites the 'low to mid single digit growth in Q3 and Q4' management needs to hold the FY guide (H2 FY25 was $3,643M; the guide implies $3,750-3,850M, i.e. +2.9% to +5.8%).
evidence.independence: Two independent, non-BLS confirmations. (1) A waterworks distributor's own customer notice: United Pipe & Steel posted a new PVC pipe list price sheet dated 5/15 stating 'PVC pipe mills have announced a list price increase' on energy/raw-material costs — https://unitedpipe.com/blog/pvc-pipe-increase-new-list-price-sheet/ (2026-05-15), which lands in week two of CNM's quarter and explains the May PPI step. (2) Plumbing & Mechanical's trade-press tally of manufacturer increases inside and after the quarter: A.Y. McDonald +6-15% eff. 7 July (https://www.pmmag.com/articles/107578-phcp-pvf-price-increases-july-2026, 2026-07-08) and American Tube & Pipe +8%, Wheatland +8%, Matco Norca +4-11%, Legend Valve +3-25% eff. August (https://www.pmmag.com/articles/107644-phcp-pvf-price-increases-august-2026, 2026-08-06). A same-publisher corroborant that should be collapsed into this cluster, not counted separately: BLS ductile iron pressure pipe PPI (WPU10150211) rose from 464.775 in Apr/May 2026 to 476.788 in Jun/Jul, +7.2% since Dec 2025 — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/WPU10150211.

evidence.text: Mueller Water Products — the largest US maker of fire hydrants and iron gate valves, sold almost entirely through waterworks distributors of which CNM is the biggest — reported its quarter ended 30 June 2026 (two of CNM's three Q2 months) on 5 August with net sales +4.1% to $395.9M driven 'primarily by higher pricing across most product lines' partially offset by slightly lower volumes, record adjusted EBITDA +24.3%, adjusted EPS +47.1%, and a third consecutive raise to FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance (to $367-372M).
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a sell-through read on the 44% of CNM's net sales that is municipal, published 34 days before CNM's print — and CNM's tape did the opposite of absorbing it, making a fresh 52-week low at $41.87 on 3 September, four weeks after MWA raised. If the read had been transferred, the run-up would not be -5.1% over 20 days and the put skew would not be positive. The specific shape MWA reported (price up, volume slightly down, margin sharply up) is exactly the distributor-favourable mix, because a distributor holding pre-increase inventory books the spread; CNM guided gross margin only to 'remain at similar levels' to Q1's 27.2%.
evidence.independence: CNM's own Q1 10-Q gives the end-market split that makes the read load-bearing (~44% municipal, 38% non-residential, 18% residential for FY ended 1 Feb 2026): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001856525/000185652526000054/cnm-20260503.htm (2026-06-10). Separately, Westlake's Q2 2026 release describes 'higher end market demand for pipe and fittings' sequentially in HIP while its PEM segment EBITDA went $36M to $416M on higher PVC resin pricing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1262823/000126282326000026/ex991_20260630earningsrele.htm (2026-08-04).

evidence.text: US single-family housing starts fell 9.9% m/m in July 2026 to an 808k SAAR, the lowest since November 2022 — a deterioration inside the final month of CNM's quarter and after management said on 10 June that residential lot development had 'largely stabilized' with 'no further deterioration'.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly it is priced — housing weakness is the consensus bear case on CNM and is the obvious reason for the -35% twelve-month decline, the two August downgrades and the bid for downside. The residual that is not priced is narrow and specific: it invalidates the exact word management used on the last call ('stabilized'), so the risk is a verbal walk-back on the lot-development commentary rather than a numbers surprise. I size it small deliberately, and it is the reason my net number is a third of the implied move rather than half.
evidence.independence: Same underlying Census release read by a second outlet: https://www.housingwire.com/articles/july-2026-housing-starts-drop-permits-rise/ — treat as one source, not two. Cutting the other way, residential is only ~18% of CNM net sales per the Q1 10-Q cited above.

evidence.text: CNM raised $750M of 6.000% senior notes due 2034 on 1 July 2026 — inside fiscal Q2 — with proceeds earmarked for prepaying the 2028 term loan and for 'general corporate purposes, including... mergers and acquisitions, share repurchases', at the same time as it had $581M left on the $1bn authorisation, had just run its highest-ever quarterly buyback ($88M / 1.8M shares in Q1 plus $37M / 0.8M shares in the five weeks to 10 June), and management flagged 'a pretty notable uptick in the pipeline... to larger opportunities' and said it might 'overperform some of our M&A goals'.
evidence.why_not_priced: The financing itself is wire copy; what is not is the combination — fresh unsecured capacity plus an untouched $1,226M ABL plus net debt down to $2,010M plus a stock that spent the back half of the quarter falling from ~$46 to a 52-week low. If a materially larger Q2 repurchase, an authorisation increase, or a sizeable acquisition were expected with the print, the stock would not be trading 4.4% off its 52-week low with an option chain whose ATM bid-ask is 72% of mid — that spread is itself evidence nobody is positioned for a capital-return catalyst. The 1 July closing also puts a loss on debt extinguishment into reported GAAP EPS but not adjusted EPS, a small headline-versus-consensus trap at the open.
evidence.independence: The buyback pace and remaining authorisation come from a different document, the Q1 press release and 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1856525/000185652526000053/cnmq12026earningspressrele.htm (2026-06-10). The M&A pipeline quotes come from the Q1 call transcript: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/10/core-and-main-cnm-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/ (2026-06-10) — note that transcript is also the source of the PVC quote in finding 1, so the two share one document and should be collapsed on that dimension.

evidence.text: Event reality: already sealed as confirmed; company PR confirms 9 Sep 2026 bmo with an 08:30 ET call, and no re-check was needed.

An unannounced large acquisition: the June/July 8-K exhibits are only the notes indenture, supplemental indenture and the Sixth Amendment $800M term loan (SOFR+175, due 2033) — no acquisition agreement, and no credible deal rumour found.

PVC pipe antitrust: CNM is named as an alleged co-conspirator, not a defendant, in In re PVC Pipe Antitrust Litigation, and I found no 2026 development that reaches CNM; the Q1 10-Q shows no material change to legal proceedings.

coreandmain.com and ir.coreandmain.com both return HTTP 403 to the fetcher, so I could not read the news archive, greenfield-opening cadence or any post-June tuck-in announcements directly from the company.

plasticstoday.com and plasticsnews.com resin-pricing pages return HTTP 403; I could not verify whether North American PVC resin rolled over in August 2026, which is the main unresolved risk to finding 1 (it would not change the quarter, which is closed and covered by the July PPI, but it would weaken the H2 guidance case). Search snippets on this were undated and I refused to use them.
Hiring signal: only aggregate open-role counts (209 on Glassdoor, 191 on Indeed) with no historical baseline — unusable as a trend.

Form 4 cluster: 13 Form 4s since 1 June (eight on 24 June, then 8 Jul, 23 Jul, 5 Aug) but EDGAR's list view would not resolve reporting owners for me, so I could not test for an insider buy at the lows; Form 144s on 27 May, 29 May and 30 June are sales and look routine.
No August or September 8-K, no pre-announcement, no guidance update, and no company statement of any kind between 2 July and the print.

The 'only two estimates' anomaly in the sweep row: the $0.919 EPS / $2.136Bn revenue consensus reconciles with broad coverage and management's own 'slight growth in the second quarter' framing — it is not a two-model artefact and there is no edge in it.

evidence.text: Sunbelt's buyback has been throttled by roughly 85%: treasury shares rose only from 3,993,501 (29 May 2026) to 4,699,397 (28 Aug 2026) — 705,896 shares in 13 weeks, ~54k/week or ~$4m/week at prevailing prices, an annualised ~$210m — versus $1,413m of buybacks in FY26 and 405,000 shares in the single week of 6-10 April 2026 under the same $1.5bn programme launched 2 March 2026; shares outstanding are flat at ~409.8m and the weekly notices show the pace decaying monotonically (405k Apr 6-10, 135k Apr 13-17, 75k Apr 27-May 1, 60k May 26-29, 60k Jun 15-18, 43k Jul 6-10, 17k Aug 10-14, 13k Aug 17-21, 23k Aug 24-28, 47k Aug 31-Sep 4).
evidence.why_not_priced: The data exists only as LSE/UK-MAR-format 'Transaction in Own Shares' / 'Share Repurchase Program - Weekly Report' notices that no US vendor parses into a time series, and nobody sums them. The coverage that does exist reads each notice as confirmation the programme is running — TipRanks headlines them 'Sunbelt Rentals Continues $1.5 Billion Buyback' and 'Boosts Treasury Stock With Ongoing $1.5 Billion Buyback', and a Simply Wall St narrative still lists 'Cash Returns And Index Support' as a pillar of fair value. If the market had done the arithmetic you would see (a) FY27 EPS estimates cut on the share-count line, because a $1.5bn programme executed on the prior 18-month cadence implies ~20m shares / ~5% of the count retired and the actual count is going nowhere (420.4m weighted diluted FY26, 412.5m in Q4 FY26, ~409.8m outstanding now), (b) the capital-return leg stripped out of bull cases, and (c) the option skew bid for downside rather than -3.35 vol points the other way. Tomorrow's 10-Q Item 5 issuer-purchase table and the diluted share count make the Q1 number explicit for the first time: roughly 250k shares / ~$19m repurchased in a quarter in which the company also closed $650m of Reliant and raised $1.2bn of notes.
evidence.independence: A different document points the same way: the FY26 Q4 press release (SEC 8-K exhibit) gives no free cash flow guidance for FY27 at all, while guiding gross rental capex UP to $2.45-2.85bn — Ashtead's practice under the old reporting regime was to give and even raise FCF guidance (it raised FY26 FCF guidance at the Q1 print on 3 Sept 2025). https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002083785/000162828026044797/sunbeltpressrelease-fy26q4.htm and https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/ashtead-q1-fy26-slides-rental-revenue-up-24-raises-free-cash-flow-guidance-93CH-4220646 . The weekly repurchase notices (detail/100, detail/122, detail/137, detail/155, detail/157 and the 2 June 2026 notice) are one source cluster and should be collapsed to one; the treasury-share balances and the per-week share counts inside them are two readings of the same filings, not independent evidence.

evidence.text: The Q1 FY27 (May-July 2026) volume setup is unusually well supported and the margin worry is pre-guided: the comp is +2.4% group rental revenue in Q1 FY26, Q4 FY26 exited at +8.0%, the $650m Reliant/Aries modular business closed 1 May 2026 so the full quarter is inorganically boosted, management flagged ~$70m of Q1-specific FIFA World Cup and UFC event revenue on the June call and said margins improve 'in the back half', and both peers reported record calendar Q2 and RAISED full-year guidance (URI rental revenue +12.7%, fleet productivity +3.4%, FY revenue guide lifted to $17.5-17.8bn from $16.9-17.4bn on 22 July; Herc rental revenue +23%, guidance raised on 28 July).
evidence.why_not_priced: The individual inputs are wire copy; what is not is that the baseline's -14.35% 20-day run-in carries essentially zero SUNB-specific information. URI is down 13.2% over the past month from an all-time-high close on 17 Aug and sits at $1,014.46 against a 52-week high of $1,179.18, i.e. -14.0% from its high on the same tape and the same macro (the 4 Sept hot payrolls print lifted rate-hike odds and hit cyclicals). So the run-in is group beta, not the market pre-positioning for a bad Sunbelt quarter. If it were company-specific de-risking you would expect puts to exist — put/call open interest is 0.02 on 16,845 total contracts and the 25-delta skew is -3.35 vol points, so nobody has actually bought downside on this name. The asymmetry is that the sell-side tone into the print is set by JPMorgan's Underweight and $71 target dated 2 Sept, which rests on a margin thesis management already telegraphed as a first-half phenomenon.
evidence.independence: Separate source, separate company: United Rentals' own Q2 2026 release (22 July 2026) https://investors.unitedrentals.com/press-releases/press-releases-details/2026/United-Rentals-Announces-Record-Second-Quarter-Results-and-Raises-Full-Year-2026-Guidance/default.aspx and Herc's Q2 2026 release via ARA's Rental Management https://news.ararental.org/herc-reports-q2-2026-results-increases-full-year-guidance ; the URI price/52-week-high anchor is https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uri/ . These are independent of the Sunbelt transcript and of the buyback filings used in finding 1.

evidence.text: S&P 500 index-committee flow: the 4 Sept 2026 S&P DJI announcement added Bloom Energy, Illumina and Everpure effective 21 Sept and did not mention SUNB (https://press.spglobal.com/2026-09-04-Bloom-Energy,-Illumina,-and-Everpure-Set-to-Join-S-P-500-Others-to-Join-S-P-100,-S-P-MidCap-400,-and-S-P-SmallCap-600); SUNB was already down to $67.11 on 3 Sept, i.e. before the announcement, so there is no 'passed-over' trade to harvest and no mechanical inclusion flow contaminating the print window

FTSE UK index deletion flow: the listing transfer and index exit happened in February 2026 (FTSE Russell informative notice 28 Jan 2026, https://research.ftserussell.com/products/index-notices/home/getnotice/?id=2618540) and SUNB is not in the September 2026 FTSE UK quarterly review (https://www.lseg.com/en/media-centre/press-releases/2026/ftse-uk-index-series-review-september-2026) — the mechanical flow the brief worried about is nine months stale
WARN notices, layoffs or branch closures for Sunbelt Rentals in 2026 — nothing found in state WARN databases or news via search
Sunbelt UK / A-Plant disposal or strategic review — no evidence of any process, despite the redomicile making a UK exit an obvious next step
CEO/CFO or senior leadership transition — leadership page and news show no change; nothing pending

Annual meeting of 1 Sept 2026 (8-K item 5.07, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2083785/000119312526380411/d55578d8k.htm): all ten directors elected, say-on-pay approved, annual frequency approved, PwC ratified — no governance dissent worth trading

Form 4 cluster: the 4 Sept 2026 disclosure is routine — 2,354 RSUs at $0.00 to each of nine directors on 1 Sept and small tax-withholding dispositions at $72.28 on 31 Aug; no open-market insider buying or selling

Used-equipment residual values: only calendar-Q1 2026 Ritchie Bros data available (US aerials/telehandlers/forklifts softer on volume, earthmoving firmer) — too stale and too mixed to say anything about the May-July quarter's disposal gains
ARA industry forecast: the August 2026 update (+3.4% US CIE and general tool rental in 2026 to $83.5bn, +4.4% in 2027) is in line with company guidance — no revision to trade
Customer-side signal: Sunbelt is B2B with no consumer app of consequence, so app-store review volume/rating and consumer forum sentiment produced nothing usable

A specific SUNB-only cause for the mid-August-to-September fall: none found beyond the group de-rate and JPMorgan's 2 Sept target cut to $71 — the Wells Fargo Overweight/$96 initiation around 17 Aug in fact marked the local high

evidence.text: Edge Retail Academy's US independent-jeweler panel shows the category decelerating sharply in August 2026 — gross sales +5% YoY (vs +18% in June and +10% in July), units -8%, average retail sale +14% — with the opening-price-point sterling silver / alternative metals category at -5% dollars and -19% units; August is month one of Signet's fiscal Q3 and the month the H2 guide has to be built on.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Edge series is published in jewelry trade press (JCK, InStore, Edge's own blog) five days before the print and is not carried by any financial wire, terminal or aggregator; Signet has only ~3 EPS estimates on the tape, so there is no sell-side machine converting a trade-press monthly into a Q3 comp. If it were priced, the 25-delta skew would not be -13.46 vol points (calls bid over puts) and Citi would not have opened a public 'upside 30-day catalyst watch' on 2026-09-08 expecting a raise to the top end of the range. The same series was benign through the quarter itself (+12/+18/+10 in May/Jun/Jul), so this is specifically a forward-guide signal, not a restatement of the Q2 print. Note the level is not transferable — Edge ran +12% in April while Signet comped +1.8% in Q1 — the sequential shape is the signal, and it is a ~7pt one-month deceleration.
evidence.independence: Two different sources point the same way on the value-end consumer: PROG Holdings' Q2 2026 call named jewelry as one of only two categories at Purchasing Power that failed to grow GMV year over year (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/prog-prg-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), and Pandora's calendar-Q2 2026 report showed North America like-for-like negative with US sales only 'stable' (https://wwd.com/accessories-news/jewelry/pandora-q2-results-2026-guidance-raised-early-announcement-1239092531/). The May/June/July Edge readings come from the same source cluster as this finding and are deliberately folded into it rather than filed separately.

evidence.text: The 15% Section 122 global import surcharge that underpinned Signet's 'mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year' expired 12:01am on 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same minute by Section 301 forced-labor duties of 10%–12.5% on the 60 economies covering Signet's sourcing base — a 2.5–5 point step down on India, the country Signet named as its principal tariff exposure, four days before its quarter ended and seven weeks after the FY27 guide was set.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a macro trade-law event that lands in the index, not in SIG's relative price; converting it requires knowing the specific sentence in Signet's 2026-06-02 call ('mid-teens effective tariff rate for the year') and that the guide was built on the 15% Section 122 number. With three estimates on the tape there is no published model of Signet's tariff line to revise. If it were priced you would see a tariff-relief note among the handful of SIG previews; instead the only visible preview thesis is Citi's generic 'inline Q2, raise to the top end', which is about demand, not landed cost. Slow-burning: Signet's ~$2.0bn inventory against ~$4bn COGS means post-July-24 landings mostly hit Q4/Q1 P&L, which is why I size it small.
evidence.independence: Jewelry-specific confirmation of the rates and effective date from National Jeweler (https://nationaljeweler.com/articles/15165-new-trump-tariffs-what-they-mean-for-jewelry), which puts India/China/Thailand/HK/UAE at 12.5% and Canada/Mexico/Pakistan/Sri Lanka/UK at 10% — note it disagrees with a 10% figure reported for India elsewhere, so I treat the step-down as 2.5–5 points rather than a point estimate. This finding and the refund finding below share the tariff theme but rest on different documents (a USTR action versus Signet's own disclosure); they should be collapsed to one residual if scored as a cluster.

evidence.text: Signet has filed IEEPA refund claims on most goods where it was importer of record and had received only 'a small amount' as of 2026-06-02, with management stating it is too early to quantify the amount or timing 'as well as how any proceeds may be used' — meaning the FY27 guide contains none of it, while CBP had already built out mass electronic IEEPA refunds covering ~82% of affected entries by April 2026, i.e. during Signet's Q2.
evidence.why_not_priced: The item is knowably excluded from guidance by the company's own words, and it is unquantifiable from outside — which is exactly why no estimate carries it and why the wire preview cannot contain it. The 'how any proceeds may be used' phrasing is a buyback tell: Signet has $355m remaining on the 2017 authorisation after a $50m ASR on 2026-06-08 and had $602.8m cash / ~$1.7bn liquidity at Q1, against a $3.2bn market cap. If the market were carrying this, the stock would not be at 8x the midpoint of a $9.20–$11.00 FY27 EPS guide and the put/call open interest ratio would not be 3.27. Wide band because the refund may land as a Q3 event, be excluded from adjusted EPS, or be deferred into contested CIT proceedings.
evidence.independence: The refund mechanism and its timing come from a different source entirely — Skadden's account of the post-Supreme-Court CBP refund process (https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/03/tariff-refund-mechanism-takes-shape) — and the buyback capacity from Signet's 2026-06-08 8-K item 8.01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/832988/000083298826000161/sig-20260608.htm). Shares the tariff theme with the finding above; different documents.

evidence.text: InnovAge's raised FY2026 guidance implies a Q4 adjusted EBITDA of only $14.7-19.7M (9M actual $70.3M = Q1 $17.6M + Q2 $22.2M + Q3 $30.495M, against a $85-90M full-year guide) and Q4 revenue of $222-247M versus Q3's $251.9M actual - i.e. a sequential revenue decline and a 4-5pp margin collapse - even though census rose to ~8,050, Colorado/state Medicaid rates are fixed through 30 June, Medicare risk scores are fixed for the calendar year, and the in-house pharmacy saving is structural; the identical structure in FY2025 (9M EBITDA $23.1M vs a $24-31M guide, implying Q4 of $0.9-7.9M) produced an actual Q4 of $11.3M and a full year of $34.5M, 11% above the top of guidance.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only two-to-three analysts cover the name and their numbers are visibly anchored to the guidance, not to the arithmetic: stockanalysis.com shows FY2026 consensus revenue of $966.07M last updated 2026-08-21, which backs into a Q4 revenue of $238.3M, a 5.4% sequential DECLINE from Q3, and the calendar's two Q4 EPS estimates of $0.09 are consistent with a ~$18-20M EBITDA quarter. No sell-side note, article or transcript question has laid out the implied Q4 step-down - the Q3 call transcript records that no analyst pressed management on it and management declined to forecast Q4. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be drifting -5.96% over 20 days into the print at exactly the $10 average analyst target; it would be marked up toward the $13 KeyBanc target set 2026-08-21.
evidence.independence: Nine-month revenue of $727.8M is confirmed independently in the 10-Q at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1834376/000183437626000022/innv-20260331.htm (filed 2026-05-08), and the Q1 FY26 $17.6M adjusted EBITDA anchor comes from a separate release at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/11/04/3180867/0/en/InnovAge-Announces-Financial-Results-for-the-Fiscal-First-Quarter-Ended-September-30-2025.html (2025-11-04). The FY2025 precedent guide of $24-31M is from a different document again, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/05/06/3075531/0/en/InnovAge-Announces-Financial-Results-for-the-Fiscal-Third-Quarter-Ended-March-31-2025.html (2025-05-06). Note the Q3 FY26 8-K exhibit and the Q3 FY26 call transcript are one source cluster with finding 2 - the transcript is supporting colour there, not independent evidence.

evidence.text: Colorado - InnovAge's home and largest state - enacted roughly $270M of Medicaid reimbursement cuts for FY2026-27, taking most fee-for-service rates down to 85% of Medicare from 2026-04-01 and layering a further 2.0% across-the-board reduction on HCBS waiver services for dates of service from 2026-07-01, published in the June 2026 provider bulletin after InnovAge last spoke to investors; PACE Medicaid capitation is set beneath an upper payment limit derived from exactly those FFS/HCBS costs, so the FY2027 Colorado rate InnovAge must build its first FY2027 guide around is flat-to-down rather than the mid-single-digit increases of prior years.
evidence.why_not_priced: The qualitative warning IS on the wire - the CFO said on 2026-05-06 that FY2027 Medicaid increases 'may be lower than what we have experienced historically' and the CEO guided Medicare to +1.5-2%. What is not on the wire is the mechanism or the size: no published note quantifies the 85%-of-Medicare reset or the 2% July-1 HCBS cut, and the July-1 piece was only confirmed in a state provider bulletin issued a month after InnovAge's last communication. If this were priced you would see a published FY2027 EBITDA estimate cut or a downgrade in the four months since the Q3 call; instead the only rated action on file is KeyBanc reiterating Buy with a $13 target on 2026-08-21 and the stock sits at the $10 average target.
evidence.independence: Independently corroborated by state budget reporting: https://www.cpr.org/2026/04/01/colorado-budget-draft-billion-shortfall-2026/ (2026-04-01, on the ~$1.5bn shortfall and the Medicaid-led cuts) and https://www.vaildaily.com/news/colorado-new-budget-cuts-medicaid/ on the signed budget. Directionally consistent with, but sourced separately from, management's own May commentary in https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/06/innovage-innv-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/ - that transcript is shared colour with finding 1 and should be collapsed to one source.

evidence.text: TCO Group Holdings (Apax and Welsh Carson) registered 112,988,070 shares - 83.2% of the 135,736,393 outstanding - for resale on a Form S-3 filed 2026-07-31 and declared effective 2026-08-05, routed there via a confidential draft registration statement submitted 2026-07-17, with no 8-K and no press release at any point; the company then scheduled FY2026 results for 2026-09-08 after the close and a Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference presentation at 08:00 ET on 2026-09-09, which is the standard sequencing for a marketed block in the window immediately after the print, and the shelf removes the Rule 144 affiliate volume cap of roughly 1.36M shares per quarter that has been the only constraint on the sponsors selling.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company never announced it - InnovAge's press-release feed runs straight from 'Jennifer Browne appointed President and COO' on 2026-05-12 to the earnings-date notice on 2026-08-26 with nothing in between, and there is no 8-K. Coverage is limited to automated SEC-filing bots. The hedging evidence is decisive: the front-expiry chain carries total open interest of 15 contracts and a put/call open-interest ratio of 0.07, so essentially nobody has bought downside protection ahead of a print that could be immediately followed by a block worth many multiples of the 175,589-share average daily volume. If a secondary overhang were priced there would be visible put demand and a negative 25-delta skew; there is no chain at all.
evidence.independence: The confidential draft is a second document under the same cluster (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1834376/000110465926084593/filename1.htm, submitted 2026-07-17) and I count it as one finding, not two. Genuinely separate corroboration of the back-to-back print-plus-conference calendar: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/26/3351255/0/en/innovage-announces-conference-call-to-discuss-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2026-financial-results-and-participation-in-upcoming-wells-fargo-healthcare-conference.html (2026-08-26). Cutting the other way, the July Form 4 cluster shows only RSU grants and no insider sales - CEO Patrick Blair took 78,397 RSUs on 2026-07-27 and holds 751,047 shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1834376/000189646326000006/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1785189578.xml), so individual insiders are not selling into strength.

A pre-published Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference deck on investor.innovage.com - the IR press-release page returned 503 repeatedly and no 8-K Item 7.01 deck has been furnished since 2026-05-18

evidence.text: Sell-side consensus for Q2 2026 is still $5.49m revenue (5 analysts, expecting +27.4% sequential growth) and -$0.16 EPS, six weeks after Nanox itself pre-announced Q2 revenue of 'approximately $4.0 to $4.1 million' -- a sequential decline; the headline on 2026-09-09 is therefore a mechanically guaranteed ~26% revenue miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the aggregator layer had ingested the 2026-07-23 pre-announcement, the Q2 consensus would sit at $4.0-4.1m and no 'miss' headline could be generated. It does not: FXEmpire still models +27.4% sequential revenue growth, and stockanalysis.com's statistics page still shows 69.60 million shares outstanding as of 2026-09-08 (the pre-August-offering count; the actual count is 78,588,638 per the Aug 7 424B5) and a $5.13 average price target on an $0.87 stock. The pre-announcement 6-K was accepted at 17:30 ET on a Thursday and the release was never carried by StockTitan's NNOX news list. On a $68m retail-dominated name with no option chain, the Zacks/Benzinga-style 'missed by 26%' print at 08:00 ET is the marginal information for most of the tape.
evidence.independence: stockanalysis.com's forecast page independently shows FY2026 consensus revenue of $25.89m from 3 analysts, against H1 2026 actual of roughly $8.4m ($4.311m Q1 + $4.0-4.1m preliminary Q2) with annual guidance formally withdrawn -- the same staleness in a second dataset: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nnox/forecast/

evidence.text: Nanox has an unquantified 'comprehensive impairment assessment across all of its assets, including but not limited to long-lived assets and goodwill' still incomplete as of 2026-08-06, sitting against $57.364m of net intangibles and $30.551m of net PP&E at 2026-03-31 -- $88.0m of impairable carrying value versus a ~$68m market cap -- and it lands in the first quarter reported by a CFO who started 2026-08-01.
evidence.why_not_priced: The impairment language appears only in the body text of the Form 6-K cover and the accompanying 424B5 prospectus supplement -- the Exhibit 99.1 press release that actually went to the wire on 2026-08-06 does not mention it at all, and no analyst note or wire story quantifies it. If it were priced, the stock would not be trading at 0.48x the post-offering book value implied by the 2026-03-31 equity of $126.308m while simultaneously bouncing +7.5% in five sessions into the print. Q1's $14.265m net loss becomes a $50-90m net loss headline (roughly -$0.7 to -$1.2 per share against a -$0.16 consensus) if a material share of that $88.0m is written down, which on this shareholder base is a shock even though it is non-cash.
evidence.independence: The $57.364m intangibles / $30.551m PP&E / $126.308m equity balances come from a different document, the Q1 press release of 2026-06-25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795251/000121390026071765/ea029511001ex99-1.htm); the CFO transition to Guy Nathanzon effective 2026-08-01 and the precedent $17.5m non-cash Korea impairment come from a third, Israel Electronics News (https://techtime.news/2026/04/23/nanox-8/). NOTE: the impairment sentence also appears in the 2026-07-23 6-K exhibit that carries the pre-announced revenue used in finding 1, so findings 1 and 2 share one source document in part and should be collapsed to their largest residual, not added.

evidence.text: The baseline's reaction history is wrong in a way that matters: the -44.01% on 2026-06-25 and -24.39% on 2026-04-20 were real earnings prints (Q1 2026 and FY2025), independently confirmed as a -43.99% post-release move, so this name's actual earnings base rate is 2-for-2 double-digit declines, not a 6.52% median.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no option chain on NNOX, so no implied move and no skew exist to encode a reaction base rate at all -- the only thing standing in for 'what is priced' here is the -18.54% 20-day run-up, and the last five sessions have run the other way (+7.51%). A market that had internalised a 2-for-2 double-digit-decline earnings record on a going-concern name would not be bidding it up 22% off the 2026-09-03 low of $0.71 into the print on a regional distributor announcement.
evidence.independence: FXEmpire independently records the 2026-06-25 release as an earnings report with a -43.99% price reaction and a -6.60% revenue miss, confirming it was an earnings event rather than an operational 6-K: https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/nnox/earnings

evidence.text: Offsetting and pointing the other way: the four things that caused the last two collapses are all already disclosed -- 2026 guidance withdrawn, going-concern doubt introduced, Korea restructuring announced with a $17.5m charge taken, and Q2 revenue and the $31.4m 6/30 cash balance pre-announced -- while management has run a positive-news cadence into the print (Intel/OpenVINO 8/10, UK reseller 8/18, New England distributor 9/4) and needs a shareholder majority on 2026-09-17 to lift authorized capital by 50m shares.
evidence.why_not_priced: The market is treating this print as a repeat of the June 25 event; it cannot be, because the new-information content is far lower -- the revenue number and the cash number are already public and the going-concern language is already in three separate 2026 filings. A market that had recognised the pre-announcement had de-risked the print would not have taken the stock from $1.11 on 2026-08-11 to $0.71 on 2026-09-03 with no company news other than an AGM proxy. Add 8.9-13.3% of the float short and management's need for a favourable tape eight days before an authorized-capital vote, and there is a real squeeze/relief branch.
evidence.independence: Short interest of 5.71m shares / 8.93% of float per stockanalysis.com (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nnox/statistics/) and the 2026-08-18 AGM proxy proposal to raise authorized capital by NIS 500,000 / 50 million shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001795251/000121390026090993/ea030243001ex99-1.htm) are separate documents supporting the same branch.

evidence.text: Nasdaq minimum-bid-price deficiency letter: no such 6-K or press release exists. Reconstructing the closes, NNOX last closed at or above $1.00 on 2026-08-14 ($1.00 exactly) and has closed below $1.00 continuously since 2026-08-17, so a 30-consecutive-business-day clock does not expire until roughly 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-01. Nothing for the Sept 9 window (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nnox/history/).

Reverse stock split: explicitly absent from the 2026-09-17 AGM agenda, which contains only director re-election, the NIS 500,000 authorized-capital increase, CEO equity grants, and auditor re-appointment. No special meeting has been called.

Korea subsidiary resolution: the Q1 release said sale / expanded consolidation / orderly wind-down were all under evaluation, and I found no Korean-language, Israeli-press or SEC disclosure of a decision since. This is the single largest genuinely open item and I could not source it either way.

Insider signal: the only Form 4 since the offering is CEO Erez Meltzer buying 9,443 shares at $1.03 on 2026-08-10, about $9.7k -- too small to read anything into. The 2026-08-04 Form 144 could not be fetched (SEC XSL endpoint timed out).
New 6-K or 8-K style disclosure between 2026-08-18 and 2026-09-08: none on EDGAR; the 2026-09-04 distributor release was not furnished as a 6-K.
RadNet's 2026-08-10 Q2 call as a customer read-through on ARC deployments: found no RadNet management commentary on Nanox, only Nanox's own characterisation of RadNet as a reference site.

ATM utilisation as a Q2/Q3 dilution driver: $53.9m of the $100m program remained as of 2026-07-23, but share count only moved 69,600,783 (3/31) to 78,588,638 (8/12), of which 8.0m is the registered direct -- so ATM issuance has been immaterial and is not the explanation for the August-September slide.
Nanox careers page for a headcount/team signal: nanox.vision returned HTTP 403.
App-store, support-forum and status-page angles: not applicable to a hospital capital-equipment and teleradiology business.

evidence.text: Lovesac told the June 11 call it had been accepted for $20.8m of IEEPA tariff refunds but had only received $3.6m, and put only that $3.6m in the Q2/FY27 guide; CBP-wide data show the payout wave ran through exactly Lovesac's fiscal Q2 (May 4 - Aug 2), with >50% of the $166bn pool repaid by July 10 and ~64% certified by Aug 21, so ~$8-15m of unguided COGS credit plausibly landed in the quarter being reported.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus of -$0.39 sits inside the company's guided net loss of -$3m to -$7m, which by the CFO's own statement excludes everything beyond the $3.6m already in hand; only two estimates cover the name, so nobody has re-marked the model for two and a half months of CBP disbursement. If the market had done the arithmetic, a $17m residual claim on a $240m equity with $57m of cash and $51.7m of unused buyback authorisation would not sit alongside the most extreme 25-delta skew in the day's universe (+30.5), a 24.85 put/call open interest ratio and 20.8% of float short. Lovesac's Q1 10-Q applies a gain-contingency model, so the credit is recognised on receipt, not accrual - which is precisely why the amount is invisible until the print.

evidence.text: DBI's Q1 10-Q discloses it sold the rights to its IEEPA tariff claims to an unnamed Investor before the 20 Feb 2026 Supreme Court ruling and expects to recognise approximately $20.0m to income (claims value less the Investor's portion, net of proceeds already received) for tariff recoveries, with no receivable booked as of 2 May 2026 because it applied the gain-contingency model — $20.0m is ~$0.36/share pre-tax on 55.9m diluted shares and ~7% of the $290m market cap, and none of it is in the FY26 $0.28-$0.38 EPS guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Gain-contingency accounting means the number appears nowhere in the Q1 press release, nowhere in the reaffirmed FY guide, and nowhere in Q1 reported or adjusted EPS — it exists only in the Commitments & Contingencies note of a 10-Q for a company with two remaining sell-side analysts (UBS Neutral, Telsey Market Perform). If it were priced, the stock would not be -16.75% over twenty sessions into a print that can mechanically deliver ~7% of market cap in cash, and previews would frame the quarter around a tariff recovery instead of quoting a garbled adjusted-EPS consensus that aggregators variously print as $0.25, $0.22 and -$0.06. The claim-sale-to-an-Investor structure is also unique to DBI among footwear names and is not something a screen surfaces.
evidence.independence: Caleres, a footwear importer whose Q2 ended 2 Aug 2026 (one day after DBI's 1 Aug quarter end), reported on 2026-09-09 that it recognised $55.6m of IEEPA tariff recoveries in cost of goods sold, which establishes that CBP CAPE payouts to footwear importers actually landed inside this exact fiscal window rather than slipping to Q3: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CAL/caleres-reports-second-quarter-2026-cbjhhvcqm4mz.html . evidence.text: DBI's FY26 guidance conservatism rests on an assumption management stated on 9 Jun 2026 — that 'a substantial portion of any potential refunds will be offset by increased risk from the new Section 301 tariffs that may begin in August' — but the August step-up replaced an expiring Section 122 10% surcharge (lapsed 24 Jul 2026) with a two-tier 10%/12.5% Section 301 forced-labour duty, an incremental 0-2.5pp rather than a new layer, and Caleres guided H2 gross margin up 150-200bp citing 'lower current tariff rates'.
evidence.why_not_priced: DBI's guide was set on 9 June against a tariff regime that had not yet been specified; the Section 122 expiry (24 Jul) and the shape of its Section 301 replacement were only settled in late July, after the last time DBI spoke publicly, so no DBI-sourced number reflects them. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be trading 30-45% below both surviving analyst targets while the only H2 downgrade in the file (UBS to $6 from $7.50 on 1 Sep 2026) is a valuation cut rather than a tariff-cost cut.
evidence.independence: Shares the Caleres 2026-09-09 release with finding 1 as corroboration and should be collapsed into that source cluster to that extent; the primary evidence here is separate (the USTR Section 301 forced-labour action and the Section 122 expiry) and is corroborated independently at https://specialtyfabricsreview.com/2026/08/14/tariffs-14/ . evidence.text: FY26 has declined at a remarkably steady rate (-11.1% Q1, -9.5% Q2, -11.6% Q3; nine months $1,210.4m, -10.3%), yet the -10%/-12% full-year guide implies Q4 revenue of $272.9m-$306.6m against a $336.6m Q4 FY25 base, i.e. -8.9% to -18.9%: simple extrapolation of the year's own run-rate lands ~$300m, at the favourable end, while a $1.50bn full-year consensus requires ~$290m (-14%), a 3-4pp step-down no quarter of FY26 has produced.
evidence.why_not_priced: Only two analysts publish on this $230m name and no earnings preview exists on the wire for 10 September (searched businesswire, stocktitan, marketbeat, gurufocus). The single reason to model a Q4 step-down is management's one sentence that the marketing-mix shift 'is expected to impact our fourth quarter performance', which has been taken at face value rather than tested against the arithmetic. If the market had done the arithmetic, the guide's low end would be visibly discounted rather than being where the published full-year consensus sits.
evidence.independence: The Q4 FY25 base of $336.6m and FY25 total of $1.69bn come from a different document, the 2025-09-04 year-end release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1084869/000143774925028327/ex_858981.htm . Industry demand for the quarter's single holiday was not a headwind: NRF put Mother's Day 2026 spend at a record $38bn with $3.2bn on flowers (https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/mother-s-day-spending-expected-hit-record-38-billion) and Colombia shipped 340m stems above the $430m of 2025 (https://colombiaone.com/2026/05/11/colombia-flowers-mothers-day-exports-2026/) — though FLWS's -18.7% Consumer Floral in the Valentine quarter shows it is a share loser, so I did not size the industry data separately.

evidence.text: The short base has not moved all year while the ability to exit has collapsed: short interest was 8,419,051 shares (27.5% of float) on 30 April 2026 and 7,754,157 (25.3%) on 14 August 2026, but days-to-cover went from 4.33 to 48.96 as average volume fell to ~200k/day, and the option chain offers no exit either (6,544 contracts total open interest, put/call OI 0.61, ATM bid-ask 67% of mid).
evidence.why_not_priced: If the squeeze asymmetry were in the price you would see puts bid over calls and a computable positive 25-delta skew; instead the baseline cannot compute a skew at all and put/call open interest is 0.61, i.e. call-heavy. You would also not see the stock drift -11.88% over 20 sessions into the print on literally zero company news — EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-05-07 and the company newsroom shows no release between 2026-05-07 and the 2026-08-19 date announcement — which reads as illiquidity and index/holder drift rather than information.
evidence.independence: The no-news claim is independent of MarketBeat: EDGAR's own filing history for CIK 0001084869 shows the last 8-K on 2026-05-07 and only routine Form 4/13G filings since (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001084869&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). The largest identifiable seller, Fund 1 Investments (Pleasant Lake Partners), did its selling on 20-22 April 2026 and reported 9.6% as of 30 June, so the April-June volume that flattered days-to-cover has gone (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1084869/000092963826003080/primary_doc.xml).

evidence.text: At the identical print one year ago the company explicitly declined to give numerical FY2026 guidance, framing the year instead as 'a pivotal period of foundation setting', and on the May 2026 call management again declined to provide any FY2027 numbers while noting the $12-13m of consultant costs expire 30 June.
evidence.why_not_priced: The two published targets sit at $5.00-$6.00 against a $3.56 spot, which requires an FY27 adjusted-EBITDA recovery off breakeven built from the ~$22m of incentive/consultant costs rolling off plus the $15-20m of incremental savings. That recovery only gets confirmed if the company guides. If the market expected a repeat of 'no numbers', the targets would not sit 40-70% above spot and the name would not be quoted as a two-analyst Strong Buy. This is the one fact in this file where a fiscal-year-end print differs structurally from the three quarterly prints that produced +3.7%, +14.6% and +16.5%.
evidence.independence: Separate source, the Q3 FY26 call transcript of 2026-05-08, records management declining FY2027 guidance and dating the consultant-cost expiry: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/08/1-800-flowers-flws-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/

evidence.text: The May 2025 credit-agreement amendment that replaced the leverage and fixed-charge tests with a minimum-liquidity covenant runs out at the fiscal quarter ending 27 December 2026, at which point the ratio covenants snap back, and the same amendment cut revolver commitments to $205m with a seasonal reduction to $125m — or $50m during the 'Affected Period' — from 1 January to 1 July each year; the FY26 10-K filed with this print has to speak to compliance across that snapback.
evidence.why_not_priced: This sits in an Item 1.01 paragraph of a sixteen-month-old 8-K attached to an earnings 8-K, and no preview, note or aggregator names the 27 December 2026 date. evidence.independence: Partially correlated with finding 3 — both are ways the FY27 setup disappoints, so treat the two negatives as one cluster rather than two independent draws. evidence.text: Alcon's contact-lens line grew 5% and Bausch + Lomb's Vision Care segment grew 4% constant-currency in the overlapping calendar quarter, and Cooper is lapping the weakest CooperVision quarter of its cycle — FQ3 FY25 CooperVision was up only 2% organically — so the CooperVision line is bounded near the 3.5-4.5% organic guide against an unusually easy comp.
evidence.why_not_priced: If the market had put weight on the peer read it would not have marked COO down 11.8% from 21 August to 9 September against Alcon's own -5.7% over the identical window, with no company news, no analyst downgrade I could find, no 8-K since 5 June and no index event (the 4 September S&P rebalance removes TAP, TTD and BLDR, not COO). A ~6pp idiosyncratic break with no locatable catalyst, while the option market stays balanced (25d skew +0.77 vol points, put/call open interest 0.37), is a tape that has priced a bad quarter the already-public peer data does not support.
evidence.independence: Bausch + Lomb's own 8-K for the same calendar quarter, from a different issuer and a different filing: Vision Care revenue $784m vs $753m, +4% constant currency — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001860742/000186074226000086/ex991q2-2026.htm (2026-08-07). Cutting the other way, National Vision reported US optical customer traffic -4.9% in the same calendar quarter (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/national-vision-q2-2026-slides-margin-gains-mask-traffic-concerns-93CH-4855352, 2026-08-2x), which is why the low end of my band is negative.

evidence.text: Cooper's own FY26 non-GAAP EPS guide of $4.58-$4.66 less the two reported halves-of-the-year quarters ($1.10 in FQ1 and $1.21 in FQ2, both from the company's press releases) leaves $2.27-$2.35 for the whole second half — i.e. H2 guided flat against H1's $2.31, when Cooper's second half is normally the seasonally stronger one, making the $1.11 FQ3 consensus a guide-anchored low bar rather than a demanding one.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus of $1.11 sits exactly on the guide's own implied H2 path, which is what you see when the sell-side is transcribing guidance rather than testing it. Cooper beat by $0.11 in FQ2 ($1.21 against a $1.10 estimate) and has beaten in each reported quarter of FY26; if the market had marked the guide as conservative, the estimate would sit above the guided path rather than on it, and the stock would not be trading 20% below its 52-week high into the print. The reported-revenue deceleration the guide contains is explained mechanically by the FX comp (H1 FY26 lapped a strong-dollar Nov-24-to-Apr-25 base and carried a ~3pp translation tailwind; H2 laps an already-weak-dollar base and carries roughly none), so the guided slowdown is a translation artefact and not a statement about the underlying business.
evidence.independence: The FQ1 half of the arithmetic comes from a separate press release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/711404/000162828026015231/cooperq12026pressrelease.htm (2026-03-05), non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.10. Note this finding and finding 1 both point positive and both ultimately rest on the same 4 June guidance event for the denominator — treat them as correlated, not as two independent votes.

evidence.text: Cooper evaluates goodwill for impairment annually during the fiscal THIRD quarter — the quarter being reported tonight — and it carries Fertility as its own standalone reporting unit inside CooperSurgical, the unit that absorbed the $324.1m LifeGlobal embryo-culture-media litigation accrual booked one quarter earlier, against $3,888.5m of group goodwill and a share price 20% off its 52-week high.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every preview of this name is written off the revenue and non-GAAP EPS lines; a goodwill charge is non-GAAP-excluded and so appears in no consensus number, which is precisely why the timing of the annual test is not something coverage tracks. If the market were carrying this, the 25-delta skew would be wider than +0.77 vol points and put open interest would exceed 0.37 of calls into a print that also happens to be the annual test date. I size it small and one-sided because the base rate is low: Cooper ran the same FQ3 test in July 2025, after the LifeGlobal recall was already public and with the stock similarly depressed, and recorded no impairment (10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-07-31). The marginal change since is one quarter's $324.1m accrual and a further de-rating, which is real but far from decisive.
evidence.independence: The Fertility-unit exposure is corroborated by a different document — the FQ2 FY26 10-Q contingencies note, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000711404/000162828026041305/coo-20260430.htm (2026-06-05) — which quantifies the accrual as '$324.1 million accrued litigation liability, partially offset by $52.5 million of insurance recoveries' and discloses over 140 lawsuits and over 1,500 claimants proffered. Caveat: the sentence establishing the third-quarter test timing is quoted from a 2022 10-Q because the fetcher could not reach the goodwill note inside the much larger FY25 10-K; I could not confirm the policy is unchanged as of FY26, and that uncertainty is inside the band.

evidence.text: A catalyst for the 24-31 August single-name break versus Alcon: no 8-K since 4 June (EDGAR shows only Form 3/Form 4 on 6 July for the new director), no downgrade found, Citi actually raised its target to $80 on 16 August, and the 4 September S&P rebalance removes TAP/TTD/BLDR with COO not mentioned anywhere in the release

evidence.text: Q1 FY26 was a 14-week quarter ($50.7m of sales) because fiscal 2026 was a 53-week year, and Q1 FY27 is 13 weeks - so the $53.2m consensus is +4.9% on the headline but roughly +13% on a per-week like-for-like basis, and management's 'moderately improve versus the prior-year period' guide is a commitment to grow through the loss of a whole selling week.
evidence.why_not_priced: No wire service, screener or estimate aggregator week-adjusts a 53-week fiscal year; the Q1 FY26 release buried it in the clause 'which included an extra week' and the $50.7m base is carried forward raw everywhere. If this were priced, the sell-side revenue estimate would sit near $49-50m (13/14ths of a flat comp) rather than $53.2m, and the pre-print commentary would frame the quarter as a like-for-like acceleration instead of a 5% YoY step-up. It sets up a release in which the YoY revenue and gross-margin comparisons understate the underlying improvement, which management will point out on the 10 Sept call.
evidence.independence: The fiscal calendar is corroborated independently by the 10-K, whose fiscal year ends 2026-05-03 against the prior 2025-04-27 - 371 days, i.e. 53 weeks: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723603/000119312526307064/culp-20260503.htm (filed 2026-07-17)

evidence.text: Culp issued its Q1 FY27 guidance on 2026-07-01 for a quarter that ended 2026-08-02 - i.e. with roughly 9 of 13 weeks already elapsed and the $7.0m tariff refund cash already in hand - so 'breakeven to positive adjusted EBITDA without the benefit of IEEPA tariff refunds' and 'net debt of approximately $5.0 million by first quarter-end' are near-observed facts, not forecasts.
evidence.why_not_priced: The baseline's expected move is a 6.02% median drawn from seven prints of which six went down - all of them delivered mid-restructuring with no forward guidance and genuinely uncertain outcomes. This print is the opposite: the guide was set two-thirds of the way through the quarter with the one-time cash already received. If the market had processed that the outcome distribution is narrow, the run-up would not be a directionless -0.58% over 20 days and the 5-day drift would not be a 17,000-share-a-day random walk; a stock about to resolve a genuinely uncertain 6% event trades differently into it. The residual is that Culp's downside tail here is much thinner than its own reaction history implies.
evidence.independence: Shares a source document with finding 3 below (the 2026-07-01 EX-99.1) - flagging the cluster. Separately corroborated by the FY26 10-K, which reports only $4.426m of full-year D&A, meaning the EBITDA-to-EPS bridge is small and the guide translates almost directly into the reported number: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723603/000119312526307064/culp-20260503.htm

evidence.text: Culp presents adjusted EBITDA and 'non-GAAP operating loss' but no adjusted-EPS line at all, so the $7.0m IEEPA refund - 16% of the $43m market cap - flows into the single headline GAAP diluted EPS figure that wires will compare directly against the $0.44 estimate, with no adjusted/GAAP mismatch to manufacture a fake miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: The default failure mode when a microcap books a one-time gain of this size is that the company headlines an ex-item loss and the tape prints a catastrophic-looking miss against a GAAP-basis estimate. That risk is real enough that if the market had checked it the estimate dispersion would show it - instead there is a single point estimate at $0.44 and no visible hedging. I checked the reconciliation captions in the company's own last release and the mismatch does not exist. This is a removed negative tail rather than new upside, which is why it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Same document as finding 2 - not independent, and the scorer should collapse these two to the larger. Nothing from a different source points the same way.

evidence.text: La-Z-Boy's fiscal Q1 ended 2026-07-25 - a window that overlaps Culp's 2026-05-04 to 2026-08-02 quarter almost exactly - showed consolidated sales down 3% to $476m with adjusted operating margin at 3.9% versus 4.8%, driven by expense deleverage on lower Wholesale and Joybird delivered sales; that is the single closest read-through to Culp's upholstery-fabrics segment, which produced $4.1m of Culp's $6.8m of Q4 gross profit.
evidence.why_not_priced: This landed on 2026-08-18, seven weeks after Culp guided and after Culp's single covering analyst set the $53.2m/$0.44 model, so it is genuinely new information relative to what is in the estimate. Culp has no options, one estimate and 17,425 shares of average daily volume - there is no mechanism by which a supplier two tiers down gets remarked on a customer's print. If it were priced, the estimate would have been cut in late August and the 20-day run-up would be negative rather than flat. It is sized small and cuts against my other findings because La-Z-Boy's written orders were the opposite signal (+16% retail written, +3% written same-store), and fabric shipments lead furniture deliveries.
evidence.independence: Same direction from ISPA's 2026 industry report, which shows US mattress unit shipments down 13.2% and market value down 6.5% year over year, bearing on Culp's bedding segment rather than upholstery: https://sleepproducts.org/2026/07/mattress-industry-trends-report-2026-overview/ (July 2026)

evidence.text: The consensus row itself - $0.44 versus -$0.02 is NOT a mis-key or a different basis. It reconciles: guided breakeven-to-positive adjusted EBITDA ex-refund, plus the $7.0m refund, less ~$1.1m quarterly D&A (FY26 total was $4.426m), less ~$0.4m interest on $19.1m of debt, taxed lightly because of the full US valuation allowance, over 12,662,784 shares = roughly $0.40-$0.48. Estimate: https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/09/07/culp-culp-expected-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-wednesday.html

Whether the $7.0m refund is new information - it is not. It was disclosed in the 2026-07-01 Q4 FY26 release with the exact dollar figure, the receipt already in Q1 FY27, and a specific net-debt-of-$5.0m quarter-end target. The stock rose 11% on that print. Fully in the wire.

A post-IEEPA tariff-relief tailwind - killed. Section 122's 10% global surcharge expired 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same day by a Section 301 forced-labour action at 10%/12.5% covering 60 economies and 99.4% of US imports, so there is no step-down in Culp's input-tariff burden going into FY27. https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2026/07/us-administration-rebuilds-global-tariff-program-under-section-301 (2026-07-27)

Whether Haiti and the Dominican Republic - Culp's sewn-mattress-cover platform, historically duty-free under CBTPA/HOPE-HELP - are swept into the new 12.5% Section 301 tier. Could not confirm either way from the published country lists, which name only 17 economies at 10% and carve out USMCA. If they are covered it is a new cost from 2026-07-24, but I will not size an unconfirmed fact.

Form 3 filed 2026-08-07 with no accompanying 8-K - chased it as a possible new 10% holder. It is Forrest E. Buck, VP Information Technology, 4,334 shares. Immaterial. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723603/000214910626000001/primary_doc.xml
The five-filing Form 4 cluster of 2026-07-20 - routine post-fiscal-year-end grant timing, no open-market buying, and no Form 4 of any kind since. No insider signal.
NC WARN notices for new Culp plant closures since 2026-07-01 - nothing found; the restructuring was declared complete and no new charge is telegraphed.
Any 8-K between 2026-07-01 and today other than the 10-K, proxy and Section 16 filings - none. No credit-facility amendment, no covenant event, no equity issuance, no management change.
