evidence.text: Q3 FY26 laps the second-weakest lemon price in eight quarters ($17.02/carton in Q3 FY25) while management said on 9 June that realised pricing was already above $20/carton and rising about $1/carton a month, yet the 3-analyst FY26 revenue consensus of $132.13M against $42.1M of actual H1 revenue implies H2 of ~$90.0M versus H2 FY25's $90.3M - i.e. the sell side is modelling H2 flat and giving no credit to either the price comp or the Sunkist volume shift into H2.
evidence.why_not_priced: It requires stitching four separate documents - the Q1 and Q2 FY26 8-K exhibits for H1 revenue and carton prices, the FY25 10-Q for Q3 FY25's $47.478M and the $17.02 carton comp, and a 3-analyst consensus that is published only as an annual number with no quarterly split anywhere. If it were priced you would see a published Q3 revenue estimate above the $47.5M year-ago figure and at least one preview note on the cadence shift; instead stockanalysis.com carries no quarter-level estimate at all and coverage is three analysts on a name turning over roughly $930k a day.
evidence.independence: Independent trade data says the same about the price direction: USDA/AMS Orlando shipping-point import prices dated 9 July 2026 show Argentine 17kg Marked Fancy lemons at $30-38 across sizes, a firm market through the middle of Limoneira's May-July quarter - https://www.indexbox.io/blog/usda-ams-orlando-shipping-point-fruit-imports-prices-report-july-9-2026/ . evidence.text: The reiterated FY26 guide of 4.0-4.5M fresh lemon cartons is arithmetically stretched: H1 FY26 delivered 681,000 (Q1, $17.41) + 1,028,000 (Q2, $16.63) = 1,709,000 cartons, down ~32% year on year, so the guide requires H2 of 2,291,000-2,791,000 against H2 FY25's 1,397,000 + 821,000 = 2,218,000 - the top end would need a Q4 (Aug-Oct, the seasonal trough) of roughly 1.9M cartons versus 821,000 last year, which the company has never done.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company has framed the H1 shortfall purely as 'cadence' and reiterated the same 4.0-4.5M range at both Q1 and Q2 without ever publishing the implied H2 requirement; nobody has done the subtraction in print. If the market had, the stock would not be 4.3% off its 52-week high going in and there would be a preview flagging guidance risk - instead the only visible sell-side action in the period was a price target trimmed to $18 from $19 that cited the Sunkist transition approvingly.
evidence.independence: Shares the same guidance arithmetic and the same two 8-K exhibits as the finding above - it is the negative half of the same document cluster, not separate evidence. evidence.text: Limoneira's lender deferred the debt service coverage ratio covenant in December 2025 so that it next resumes 'measurement as of October 31, 2026' at 1.25:1.0 - six weeks after the fiscal year the company is now two-thirds through - against H1 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of minus $9.4M (Q1 -$7.7M, Q2 -$1.7M), FY25 full-year adjusted EBITDA of minus $6.452M, total debt of $94,120,000, cash of $891,000 and only $22,096,000 of remaining revolver capacity.

evidence.text: AEO's fiscal 2026 guidance is built on 'a tariff rate of 10% for second quarter receipts and 15% for the back-half of the fiscal year' (set 2026-05-28, reaffirmed 2026-07-01), but the Section 122 10% surcharge expired at its 150-day limit on 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same day by a Section 301 forced-labor tariff of 10% base / 12.5% for a 46-economy higher tier that includes Vietnam, China and Thailand — so AEO's actual blended back-half rate on a Vietnam/Bangladesh/India/Cambodia/Indonesia sourcing base is roughly 10.5-12%, not 15%, and the company has not publicly revised the assumption since the regime changed.
evidence.why_not_priced: The preview literature is still quoting the 15% back-half rate as fact and framing it as the central risk — a 2026-09-08 preview is titled 'American Eagle Needs 81% Of Its Year In The Back Half — While The Tariff Rate Steps Up' and builds its whole bear case on the 10%-to-15% step-up, one day before the print. If the market had reconciled AEO's May assumption against the July 24 statutory replacement, that preview could not have been written that way, the 25-delta skew would not be +6.6 puts-bid, and the stock would not be trading 38.9% below its 52-week high on a plan whose largest stated cost headwind is roughly 3-4 points of receipt value lighter than budgeted. AEO set the number before the regime existed and reaffirmed it on 2026-07-01, three weeks before the change.
evidence.independence: Independent confirmation of the same regime change from a different publisher: https://www.tariffstool.com/tariffs-from-vietnam (last updated 2026-08-24) states Vietnam is 12.5% under the Section 301 forced-labor tariff effective 2026-07-24, replacing Section 122. The company-side anchor is a separate document, https://www.aeo-inc.com/2026/05/28/american-eagle-outfitters-reports-first-quarter-results-5/ (2026-05-28), whose guidance footnote states the 10%/15% assumption.

evidence.text: AEO will report GAAP EPS several times the $0.21 consensus purely mechanically — it told CNBC on 2026-06-03 it had already received $108m of IEEPA refunds, its 10-Q says the amount plus any further refunds will be recorded as a reduction of cost of sales for the 13 weeks ending 2026-08-01, and guidance explicitly excludes it — but the 2Q26 retail season's own base rate is that the market strips these out: Kohl's fell about 6% on a $150m refund and a raised full-year outlook, Target's stock fell on a beat containing $1.65/share of refund, and the only large positive reaction (ANF +36%) came with a 23% underlying beat ex-refund.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a correction to a mispricing of the *reaction function*, not of the fact. AEO's own tape shows the read-across is unresolved: the stock rose 5.14% on 2026-08-26 (ANF's refund-driven print) and gave back 5.12% on 2026-08-27, a clean round trip to zero, and the 20-day run-up is -0.78%. That pattern is what an unsettled question looks like, not a priced one. If the market had settled it in the bullish direction the run-up would be positive and the skew would be call-bid; if it had settled it bearishly there would be no 5% up-day. The consequence is that the near-certain 3x headline beat is not the catalyst a naive reading of the six-estimate consensus implies, and the resulting full-year operating-income raise from ~$390-410m to ~$500m+ will be discounted as a non-recurring item that has to be lapped in 2027.
evidence.independence: Coresight's 2026-09-08 survey of 2Q26 refund bookings and the guidance split across Walmart, Target, TJX, Ross, Dollar Tree, Dollar General, Lululemon, Deckers, Crocs and Levi's points the same way from a different publisher: https://coresight.com/research/tariff-refunds-in-2q26-billions-booked-by-retailers-and-brands-guidance-split/ . The AEO-specific refund fact is from a separate source again, https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/06/03/american-eagle-outfitters-says-it-has-received-108-million-in-tariff-refunds-so-far.html (2026-06-03).

evidence.text: Ravi Thanawala became AEO's CFO effective 2026-08-03 — two days after the quarter being reported closed on 2026-08-01 — succeeding Mike Mathias after 25 years, and tonight is his first earnings call; he inherits, without having set it, a full-year plan whose arithmetic requires $324.5m of the $390-410m operating-income guide (81.1%) to land in the back half, a 4.3x ramp off $75.5m of first-half operating income.
evidence.why_not_priced: The CFO change was covered as a personnel story in early July and has not been connected to the shape of the guide it lands on top of. Every preview I found — including the 2026-09-08 one that does the 81.1% arithmetic — treats the back-half loading as a pure operating question and does not mention that the person who now owns that number started 37 days ago and did not build it. If the market had connected them, the coverage would frame tonight as a rebasing event rather than a beat-or-miss on $0.21, and a stock 38.9% off its high with a plan needing a 4.3x second-half ramp would carry more than a 6.6-point 25-delta skew on 188% ATM implied vol, which is proportionally flat for an event of this kind. Note the offset that is genuinely priced: the company reaffirmed both Q2 and full-year guidance in this same release on 2026-07-01, which caps how bad the Q2 underlying can plausibly be.
evidence.independence: The 81.1% back-half arithmetic is from a different source and a different date: https://tradesandgains.substack.com/p/american-eagle-needs-81-of-its-year (2026-09-08), which computes $75.5m first-half versus $324.5m implied second-half operating income. Peer evidence that the back-half consumer is not obliging is separate again — ANF's Hollister comps -3% and Gap comps -1% over the identical weeks (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/26/3351233/0/en/abercrombie-fitch-co-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results.html, 2026-08-26). This finding shares the May 28 guidance document as background with finding 1, but rests on a different primary document (the July 1 8-K exhibit) and cuts the opposite way.

evidence.text: BofA's reinstatement at Underperform with a $16 price objective, citing Bloomberg Second Measure data showing American Eagle brand sales -15% year over year in the week ending August 2 against Aerie +12% and OFFLINE +29% — the only URL I could reach for it (https://www.thestreet.com/retail/american-eagle-stock-bofa-aerie-growth-retail-clothes-shopping-change) returned HTTP 403 and carries no year in its path, and I could not confirm from the document itself whether it is August 2026 or August 2025. evidence.text: Macy's told the Street on 2026-06-04 that IEEPA tariff refunds are 'not incorporated in our outlook', yet both department stores with the identical quarter-end (1 Aug 2026) booked large refunds in that quarter — Kohl's ~$150m received, ~$100m through gross margin; Dillard's $37.2m, $1.82/share — and both stocks fell or went nowhere on the resulting monster beats, so the near-certain headline beat at Macy's is worth roughly nothing and possibly less than nothing to the price.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q2 consensus of $0.37 embeds a 9.8% YoY EPS *decline* and the Zacks metric detail published 2026-09-04 carries no refund line at all; the investing.com preview published this morning (2026-09-09) contains zero mentions of tariff refunds, Kohl's or Dillard's. If the read-across were priced, consensus would not still be modelling a YoY decline and the FY Street number would not sit at $2.23 against a company guide of $2.00-$2.20. The unpriced part is not the beat — it is the reaction function: at -15.7 vol points of skew the option market is paying up for calls into a catalyst whose two nearest analogues, three and four weeks ago, produced -3.5% and -0.1% because both were punished on the top line while the one-time gain was discounted entirely. Second-order risk in the same cluster and pointing the same way: the CIT's July order gives a confirmed refund path only to importers that sued, Macy's is not identifiable among the CIT plaintiffs and its own language was that 'timing and amounts remain uncertain' — so Macy's may book materially less than the ~$0.24 Jefferies has publicly penciled in, or nothing, while peers banked theirs.
evidence.independence: Dillard's 8-K/release of 2026-08-13 quantifies the same catalyst independently at $37.2m ($1.82/share) with the stock closing down ~3.5% that day: https://investor.dillards.com/news-releases/news-release-details/dillards-inc-reports-second-quarter-and-year-date-results-3 . Separately, Holland & Knight (2026-07-27) documents that non-plaintiff importers have no confirmed refund path: https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/07/file-now-cits-order-confirms-only-importers-that-have-sued . These are different documents from the Kohl's 8-K but sit in one tariff-refund source cluster with it — treat as one finding, not three.

evidence.text: Sell-side models Q2 credit card revenue at $166.2m, +8.6% YoY, but management guided on 2026-06-04 that credit card growth would decelerate to 'more in line with the overall business' — roughly +1% to +2% on a $153m base, i.e. about $156m — a ~$10m gap on a line that drops straight to EBIT in a quarter consensus puts at only ~$0.37 of EPS.
evidence.why_not_priced: The consensus line item is published (Zacks, 2026-09-04) at +8.6% while the company's own stated forward growth rate is low single digit; if the market had reconciled the two, the modelled 'other revenue' of $200.2m would have been marked down toward the FY $920m other-revenue guide's implied run-rate rather than extrapolating Q1's +11.7%. Nobody writes previews off a guidance verb ('more in line with the overall business') because it carries no number, which is exactly why it survives unmodelled.
evidence.independence: Consensus segment detail from a different source, Zacks via Yahoo 2026-09-04: https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/wall-streets-insights-key-metrics-131503279.html . No third source corroborates the deceleration; Citi's own card master-trust delinquency and charge-off data (July 2026: delinquencies 1.32%, NCO 1.90%) shows portfolio credit still benign, which cuts the other way and is why the band is wide and the size small.

evidence.text: Citi credit-card master-trust monthly delinquency/charge-off series as a lead on the Macy's profit share — the trust that files publicly is Citi's own branded-card Issuance Trust, not the Citi Retail Services private-label book that houses Macy's, and the published July 2026 data (delinquencies 1.32%, NCO 1.90%) shows nothing deteriorating; the door named as the best one in the brief is not actually mapped to this line
Renewed Arkhouse/Brigade takeover activity — everything found dates to 2024 and mid-2025, nothing in 2026, so the -15.7 calls-bid skew is not explained by a live bid
Macy's 8-K filings since 2026-06-03 — there are none; no pre-announcement, no material event, no quiet 8-K
Insider Form 4 clusters — only routine director RSU/phantom grants and one SVP/controller sale of 10,077 shares at $25.63 on 2026-06-25; no buying cluster

Macy's as a named plaintiff in the CIT IEEPA refund litigation — could not confirm either way from public search, which is itself the reason the refund size is uncertain rather than a finding on its own
Real-estate/asset-sale gains as a swing factor — Q1 2026 was $15m against Q2 2025's $16m and Q2 2024's $36m, no evidence of a lumpy Q2 2026 monetisation
A company-specific cause for the -8.1% 20-day drawdown — general-merchandise retail is down ~5.6% over the same month, so most of it is sector beta, not a Macy's signal
Census department-store-specific sales for May-July 2026 — only the headline retail aggregate was retrievable (June +0.2% m/m, July -0.6% m/m), no department-store line

evidence.text: Imperial sold its 2007-built 160,000 dwt suezmax Suez Enchanted for ~$49m with no press release and no 6-K, so year-over-year fleet deadweight is flat (1,195,000 dwt in the 2025-09-05 boilerplate vs 1,197,000 dwt in the 2026-09-04 boilerplate, +0.17%) while basic shares went from ~35.6m (Q2 2025: $12.8m net income / $0.36 EPS) to 45.21m, i.e. per-share carrying capacity fell ~21% in a year.
evidence.why_not_priced: The company issued a dedicated press release when it BOUGHT these two suezmaxes in 2022 and when it SOLD its aframax in 2023, but issued none here; EDGAR shows no 6-K at all between 2026-05-22 and 2026-08-28, and the 2026-08-28 6-K is only the proxy plus 2025 audited statements. The only public traces are a paywalled shipping trade item and a changed line in the 'About Imperial Petroleum' boilerplate. If the market had processed it, StockTitan's headline on the 2026-09-04 release would not read 'A 25-vessel fleet could follow contracted ship purchases at Imperial Petroleum' - the aggregators read a disposal as growth. Management also said nothing about any vessel sale on the 2026-05-22 Q1 call, so the disposal post-dates every piece of coverage the market has.
evidence.independence: The boilerplate diff itself is a second, independent confirmation of the same disposal: 2026-05-19 says 'twenty-one vessels on the water - seven M.R. product tankers, two suezmax tankers, four handysize drybulk carriers...approximately 1,324,000 dwt' (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/19/3297643/0/en/Imperial-Petroleum-Inc-Announces-the-Date-for-the-Release-of-the-First-Qurarter-2026-Financial-and-Operating-Results-Conference-Call-and-Webcast.html) versus 2026-09-04 'one suezmax tanker, five handysize...approximately 1,197,000 dwt' (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/04/3356593/0/en/imperial-petroleum-inc-announces-the-date-for-the-release-of-the-second-quarter-and-six-months-2026-financial-and-operating-results-conference-call-and-webcast.html). Share count 45.21m from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/impp/statistics/ (2026-09-09); the ~35.6m 2025 base is derived from the 2025-09-05 Q2 2025 release. NOTE: finding 3 below reads a different number off the same two boilerplates and should be treated as one source cluster with this one.

evidence.text: The forward half of tomorrow's print is materially worse than the backward half: MR and LR1 spot was assessed at mid-$20k/day in late July against a $49,551/day Q2 2026 MR average, and management disclosed on the Q1 call that $130m of vessel purchase obligations remain ($52m due through end of Q3 2026, $78m by end-2026/early-2027) against $212.6m of cash - so the retail 'cash exceeds market cap' premise is roughly 60% pre-spent.
evidence.why_not_priced: IMPP has zero sell-side coverage (stockanalysis.com shows no analysts), so there is no preview, no consensus and no published net-cash-after-commitments figure for this name; the $130m obligation schedule exists only inside a Q1 conference-call transcript, not in any press release or aggregator field. If it were priced, the stock would not have run +17.8% in twenty sessions into a quarter whose sequential follow-through is a halving of the rate that drives seven of its eight tankers, and the widely-shared retail write-up would not still be quoting an unencumbered ~$246m cash pile.
evidence.independence: Separate confirmation of the capex schedule and the cash figure from the company's own Q1 2026 call, a different document and different publisher: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/22/impp-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/ (2026-05-22), where management says '$52 million is expected to be paid through the end of Q3 26, while the remaining $78 million is due by the end of 26 or early 27'. Also independent: cash of $212.6m at 2026-03-31 was essentially unchanged from $212.2m at 2025-06-30 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/05/3145289/0/en/Imperial-Petroleum-Inc-Reports-Second-Quarter-and-Six-Months-2025-Financial-and-Operating-Results.html), i.e. a year of record earnings produced no cash build.

evidence.text: The vessel delivery schedule management committed to has already failed: the 2026-05-19 boilerplate had 21 vessels on the water and five contracted for delivery 'by end of Q3 26', and the 2026-09-04 boilerplate still shows 21 on the water with four still contracted - one handysize arrived in three and a half months, with three weeks of Q3 left.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nothing aggregates a company's own boilerplate against the same boilerplate four months earlier, and the release that carries it is filed as a routine date announcement that no wire service reads for content. If the slippage were priced there would be coverage of a delayed fleet ramp; instead the only headline written about this release describes fleet growth to 25 ships.
evidence.independence: Shares the same two boilerplate documents as finding 1 - treat as one source cluster. Corroborating but non-independent: management's 'five more vessels contracted for delivery through Q3 2026' on https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/22/impp-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/ (2026-05-22).

evidence.text: Q2 2026 is arithmetically near-certain to be Imperial's best quarter ever by a wide margin - Q1 2026 delivered $28.0m net income and $0.60 EPS on an average 19.88 vessels with only about one month of the rate spike, whereas Q2 ran ~21 vessels with MR spot averaging $49,551/day, both suezmaxes on spot in a record crude market, and supramax averaging above $17,000/day (best since 2022), against a Q2 2025 base of $36.3m revenue and $12.8m net income - and no equity offering has been filed since the 2025-12-01 424B5.
evidence.why_not_priced: With no analyst coverage there is no consensus EPS for IMPP, so no one has published the per-share arithmetic that a quarter of roughly $1.00-1.30 of EPS on a $5.335 stock implies; 'tanker rates were good' is the sector framing and does not convey that magnitude. The absence of dilution is checkable only on EDGAR: for a serial issuer, three and a half months with no 424B5 and no 6-K between 2026-05-22 and 2026-08-28 removes the single most reliable historical bear catalyst on this name.
evidence.independence: Peer confirmation from different companies and different publishers that Q2 2026 was an all-time record tanker quarter: Scorpio Tankers record Q2 profit and $1.3bn net cash (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/scorpio-tankers-q2-2026-slides-record-profit-13b-net-cash-93CH-4824617) and Teekay Tankers record quarterly adjusted earnings on historic-high spot rates (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/08/03/teekay-tankers-q2-earnings-call-highlights.html, 2026-08-03). EDGAR filing index for the no-offering point: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001876581.json.

evidence.text: The Q1 FY27 10-Q says the gain on the HPFR/HiViz sale attributable to inventory Lakeland still manufactures and ships for the buyer 'has been deferred and will be recognized over the six-month contract period' (27 Mar - 27 Sep 2026) — so a further tranche of divestiture gain lands inside fiscal Q2 (May-Jul 2026) on top of the $6,467k already booked in Q1, and the single published estimate is -$0.05.
evidence.why_not_priced: The mechanic exists only in one sentence of a business-combination/disposal note; no wire story, no press release and no transcript quantifies the deferred portion. If it were priced the single estimate would not sit at -$0.0475 GAAP, and the Q1 coverage would have flagged that the $0.04 of Q1 'net income' was entirely a $6.5m asset-sale gain (ex-gain operating loss ~$4.2m vs -$4.6m prior year) rather than reporting a turnaround. On a 48,885-share ADV name the first print reaction is driven by the headline EPS line.
evidence.independence: The size and existence of the gain is corroborated independently by the Q4/Q1 call commentary ($14m proceeds, $6.5m gain): https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/09/lakeland-lake-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/ . Note this finding and the covenant finding both touch the same 10-Q document — they are separate paragraphs (disposal note vs credit-agreement note) but share the filing.

evidence.text: The reaffirmed FY27 'high single-digit revenue growth' target is arithmetically out of reach: FY26 was $192.6m, Q1 FY27 was $47.4m (+1.4%) and the Q2 estimate is $51.48m (-2% vs the $52.5m year-ago quarter), so H1 is ~$99m and H2 must deliver ~$107m against H2 FY26's $93.4m, i.e. ~+15%, with the divested HPFR/HiViz lines absent from the whole second half.
evidence.why_not_priced: No aggregator carries a quarterly revenue series for this name — the number has to be built from four separate releases (Q1 FY26 $46.7m, Q2 FY26 $52.5m, Q4 FY26 $45.8m, FY26 $192.6m implying Q3 $47.6m). The one covering analyst has a Buy and raised the target to $18 on 11 June 2026 against an $11.33 spot; if the H2 ramp were understood as a stretch that target would not be 59% above the price. A guidance trim on this call reads to the tape as a cut, not as arithmetic anyone had already done.
evidence.independence: Management themselves pre-framed Q2 as 'a stepping stone rather than the full measure of the improvement opportunity' with the improvement in H2, which is the same H2-loaded shape: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/09/lakeland-lake-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/ (2026-06-09). Points the same direction as the MSA finding below on revenue, but via a different mechanism and a different source.

evidence.text: MSA Safety, the largest fire-service PPE competitor, said on 30 July 2026 that fire-service orders tied to Assistance to Firefighters Grants 'came in more slowly than expected' in the quarter with fire-service revenue slightly down year on year — a read on Lakeland's single largest product line (49% of revenue) covering almost exactly Lakeland's fiscal Q2 (May-Jul 2026), and issued seven weeks after Lakeland last spoke.
evidence.why_not_priced: MSA is a $9bn NYSE industrial and Lakeland a ~$115m Nasdaq microcap with one covering analyst; the read-across is never written up. If it had been priced, LAKE's 20-day run-up would not be only -6.75% and the Q2 revenue estimate would have moved off $51.48m, which implies roughly +7-10% organic growth once the divested HPFR/HiViz lines are stripped from the $52.5m comp — the opposite of what MSA described. The offsetting half (MSA said June/July momentum improved and FEMA wants to accelerate 2026 grant deliveries) is why this is sized under the implied-move scale rather than at it.
evidence.independence: The underlying grant-cycle slippage is independently visible in FEMA's own calendar: the FY2025 AFG application window did not open until 19 May 2026, pushing grant-funded turnout-gear awards out by roughly a year — https://www.fema.gov/press-release/20260518/dhs-makes-648-million-available-help-firefighters-and-first-responders (2026-05-18).

evidence.text: Lakeland was out of compliance with its revolver covenants at 31 Jan 2026 and needed a limited waiver; the 10-Q sets the funded-debt/EBITDA cap at 3.5x stepping down to 3.25x on 1 Feb 2026 and 3.0x on 1 Feb 2027, and at 30 Apr 2026 the $23.8m drawn against ~$7.7m LTM adjusted EBITDA ex-FX (Q2 FY26 $5.1m + Q3 $0.2m + Q4 $1.3m + Q1 FY27 $1.1m) is ~3.1x — but the $5.1m quarter rolls out of LTM at 31 July, and no 8-K has been filed since 18 June 2026 despite management saying in June they were pursuing an asset-based lending replacement.
evidence.why_not_priced: The waiver disclosure sits in the FY26 results release and the covenant step-down schedule in the 10-Q; connecting them to the quarterly adjusted-EBITDA series is arithmetic nobody publishes for a name with one analyst. If the market had priced a second covenant event the stock would not be +49% off its 52-week low, and the absence of any 8-K since 18 June — with a material new credit facility being an Item 1.01 event — would have been noticed. This is the lowest-confidence item here: management said in April they 'anticipate to be in covenant throughout fiscal 2027', covenant EBITDA has add-backs I cannot see, and $13.2m of divestiture proceeds plus $5.8m of Q1 operating cash could have paid the revolver down.
evidence.independence: The waiver itself is confirmed from a different document, the FY26 results release: 'As of January 31, 2026, the Company was not in compliance with certain covenants under its revolving credit agreement. After January 31, 2026, the Company received a limited waiver' — https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/04/16/3275796/0/en/lakeland-fire-safety-reports-fiscal-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2026-financial-results.html (2026-04-16). Shares the 10-Q with finding 1.

evidence.text: Insider Form 4s: the three 2026-08-04 and four 2026-07-13 filings are code-F tax withholding at ~$11.40, not an open-market cluster in either direction
13G/A filings: BlackRock at 1.6% and Royce at 13.37%, both with a 30 June 2026 event date, i.e. routine quarterly amendments, not an off-cycle exit
No 8-K of any kind since 2026-06-18 — no pre-announcement, no credit amendment, no executive change, no acquisition; the 2026-06-18 8-K is only the 2026 equity plan and clean annual-meeting votes
The 2026-09-01 investor-conference release contains no business or financial update
No CEO/CFO transition: Jenkins has held President/CEO plus Executive Chairman since 2024/2023, so the 'CEO/Executive Chairman' styling in the September release is not new

Could not source a dollar figure for HPFR/HiViz product-line revenue — the FY26 10-K, the Q1 FY27 10-Q, both earnings releases and both transcripts disclose $14m of proceeds and a $6.5m gain but never the revenue being removed

PFAS: only a $0.064m adjustment in Q1 FY27 and no new litigation disclosure; NFPA 1970 recertification deadline of 18 March 2026 has passed and management frames the standard change as demand-positive, not as a liability
